para.heading: Residential-care facility (Age-restricted).
para.text: See "Age-restricted residential-care facility".

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Resource recovery facility" means, except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, a facility that:
processes solid waste to produce valuable resources, such as steam, electricity, or refuse-derived fuel; and
achieves a volume reduction of at least 50% of the waste that is being processed.

para.heading: Exclusions.
para.text: "Resource recovery facility" does not include:
any facility that processes hazardous materials;
any facility that is licensed by the State or City as a junk dealer, scrap metal processor, or scrap metal dealer; or
any junk or scrap storage and yard.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Restaurant" means an establishment at which:
food and drinks are provided to the public, primarily for on-premises consumption by seated patrons; and
if the establishment also serves alcoholic beverages:
a full menu of food and drinks is prepared primarily on premises; and

annually, the average daily receipts from the sale of food exceeds 50% of the establishment's total average daily receipts, not including sales of novelty items, income from vending machines, cover charges, or other receipts not derived from the sale of food or beverages.

para.heading: Exclusions.
para.text: "Restaurant" does not include a carry-out food shop.

para.heading: Retail: Big Box Establishment.
para.text: "Retail: Big Box Establishment" means any single-use commercial building, whether stand-alone or within a multi-building development, which single-use building occupies at least 75,000 square feet of gross floor area.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Retail goods establishment" means an establishment that sells goods, wares, or other merchandise directly to consumers.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Retail goods establishment", as applied to a delicatessen, bakery, grocery, or similar establishment that sells ready-to-eat food products, includes incidental seating areas for consumption of food on the premises.

para.heading: Exclusions.
para.text: "Retail goods establishment" does not include any heavy sales, rental, or service establishment.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Right-of-way" means land dedicated for use as a public way.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Right-of-way" includes the roadway and, generally, the curbs, parkways, sidewalks, lighting facilities, and drainage facilities.

para.heading: Roof deck.
para.text: "Roof deck" means a roofless outdoor platform that is constructed on the roof of a structure and connected to the roof by structural supports.

para.heading: Roofline.
para.text: "Roofline" means the top edge of a roof or building parapet, whichever is higher, excluding any cupolas, pylons, chimneys, or minor projections.

para.heading: "Rooming unit" defined.
para.text: In this section, "rooming unit" means any room or group of rooms that forms a single habitable unit occupied or designed or intended to be occupied for sleeping or living purposes, but not for cooking purposes.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Rooming house" means a building that:
is not a dwelling;

contains 3 or more rooming units occupied or designed or intended to be occupied as a primary residence by individuals who, even though they do share common areas and facilities, do not form a single housekeeping unit and do not provide compensation under a single lease for occupancy of the facility; and
provides shared facilities such as a kitchen and bath.

para.heading: Rowhouse.
para.text: See "Dwelling: Rowhouse".

para.heading: Satellite dish antenna.
para.text: "Satellite dish antenna" means a dish antenna for transmitting signals to a receiver or receiving station or for receiving television, radio, data, communication, or other signals from satellites or from other antennas or services.

para.heading: Seasonal or holiday sales lot.
para.text: "Seasonal or holiday sales lot" means a temporary retail sales operation, generally conducted outdoors, that offers for sale seasonal or holiday related items, such as Christmas trees and pumpkins.

para.heading: Semi-detached dwelling.
para.text: See "Dwelling: Semi-detached".

para.heading: Shielded lighting.
para.text: See "Lighting: Shielded".

para.heading: Shipyard.
para.text: "Shipyard" means any facility or area that is designed or used for the manufacture, assembly, or repair of ships, barges, or boats.

para.heading: Side lot line.
para.text: See "Lot line: Side".

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Sign" means any writing (including letter, word, or numeral), pictorial representation (including illustration or graphic), emblem (including logo, symbol, or trademark), device, or any other figure of similar character that:

is attached to, painted on, projected on, or in any other way represented on a structure, in or on a window (including anything affixed to the interior and displayed within 12 inches of a window), or on the ground;
is used to announce, direct attention, or advertise; and
is visible from outside a structure.

para.heading: Types of signs.
para.text: Specific types of signs are as described in § 17-102 {"Signs: Definitions"} of this Code.

para.heading: Significant development.
para.text: "Significant development", as it applies to the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, has the meaning stated in § 7-402 {"CBCA Overlay: Definitions"} of this Code.

para.heading: Social club.
para.text: See "Lodge or social club".

para.heading: Solid waste sanitary landfill.
para.text: See "Landfill: Solid waste sanitary".

para.heading: Special exception.
para.text: See "Use: Conditional".

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Stadium" means a structure with tiers of seats rising around a field or court, intended to be used:
primarily for the viewing of athletic events; and
secondarily, for entertainment and other public gathering purposes, such as conventions, circuses, or concerts.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Stadium" includes the following accessory uses designed and intended primarily for patrons of the facility:
a gift or souvenir shop; and
a restaurant or refreshment stands.

para.heading: Stacking space.
para.text: "Stacking space" means a space specifically designated as a waiting area for vehicles patronizing a drive-through establishment.

para.heading: Stormwater.
para.text: "Stormwater" means the water running off the surface of a drainage area during and immediately following rain or as a result of other precipitation.

para.heading: Story.
para.text: "Story" means that portion of a building, other than a basement, that is:
included between the surface of any floor and the surface of the floor next above it; or
if there is no floor above it, then the space between the floor and the ceiling next above it.

para.heading: Structural alteration.
para.text: "Structural alteration" means:
a change in the permanent physical members of a structure, such as bearing walls, columns, beams, or girders; or
any substantial change in the roof or in the exterior walls.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Structure" means all or any part of anything erected that:
has a fixed location on the ground; or
is attached to something having a fixed location on the ground.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Structure" includes any building, fence, wall, sign, or tower.

para.heading: Structure: Accessory.
para.text: See "Accessory structure".

para.heading: Substantial construction.
para.text: "Substantial construction" means:
for new construction, that construction materials have been placed in permanent positions or fastened in a permanent manner; or
in preparation for rebuilding, that excavation, demolition, or removal of an existing structure has been substantially begun and is carried on diligently.

annotations.annotation: For the Code-wide standard definition of “street”, see City General Provisions Article, § 1-109, .

para.heading: Tavern.
para.text: "Tavern" means a business establishment that:
is devoted primarily to serving alcoholic beverages to the public for on-premises consumption; and
might or might not also:
serve food; and
sell alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption.

para.heading: Through lot.
para.text: See "Lot: Through".

para.heading: Transparency (of facade).
para.text: "Transparency", when used in reference to a building's facade, means the percentage of the facade that consists of glass.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Truck repair" means an establishment that is engaged in the repair and servicing of trucks.

para.heading: "Truck" defined.
para.text: In this subsection, "truck" means a commercial vehicle of more than 10,000 pounds gross vehicle weight.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Truck stop" means a facility primarily for the retail sale of fuel for commercial vehicles.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Truck stop" includes:
incidental repair or servicing of commercial vehicles; and
facilities for parking and for drivers to eat and rest.

para.heading: Truck terminal.
para.text: "Truck terminal" means a facility primarily:
to accommodate the transfer of goods to trucks, truck trailers, or other vehicles; or
to accommodate the parking or storage of commercial vehicles or trailers.

para.heading: Unshielded lighting.
para.text: See "Lighting: Unshielded".

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Urban agriculture" means the cultivation, processing, and marketing of food, with a primary emphasis on operating as a business enterprise.
"Urban agriculture" includes:
animal husbandry;
aquaculture;
agro-forestry;
vineyards and wineries; and
horticulture.
"Urban agriculture" might involve the use of:
intensive production methods;
structures for extended growing seasons;
on-site sale of produce; and
composting.

para.heading: Use.
para.text: "Use" means:
any purpose for which land or a structure is used, occupied, or intended to be used or occupied; and
any activity, occupation, business, or operation that is carried out on land or in a structure.

para.heading: Use: Accessory.
para.text: See "Accessory use".

para.heading: Use: Conditional.
para.text: "Use: Conditional" means a use that:
may be authorized by the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or, if required by this Code, by Ordinance of the Mayor and City Council as a special exception under the State Land Use Article; and
is subject to review and approval by the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or by the Mayor and City Council, as the case may be, and the imposition of conditions or restrictions under this Code.

para.heading: Single-family dwelling.
para.text: See "Dwelling: Single-family".

para.heading: Use: Permitted.
para.text: "Use: Permitted" means a use allowed in a zoning district without the need for special administrative review and approval, as long as it conforms to all the applicable requirements and standards of this Code.

para.heading: Use: Principal.
para.text: "Use: Principal" means the main use of land or a structure, as distinguished from an accessory use.

para.heading: Utilities.
para.text: "Utilities" includes:
natural gas lines, power lines, alternative energy systems, steamlines, telephone lines, cable television lines, fiber optic lines, and other communication lines;
above ground private utility structures, such as pedestals for cable wire access or other access points for underground infrastructure (communications wiring or fiber optic);
appurtenances and components of these; and
the operation, maintenance, repair, and replacement of these.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Vehicle dismantling facility" means an establishment for the buying, selling, trading, storing, or otherwise dealing in vehicles for the purpose of dismantling the vehicles and buying, selling, storing, or trading their integral parts or component materials.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Vehicle dismantling facility" includes pull-or-pick-apart facilities, salvage pools, salvage auctions, and businesses and individuals that handle salvage vehicles.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Video lottery facility" means a facility that has been awarded a Video Lottery Operation License by the Maryland Video Lottery Location Commission under State Government Article, Title 9, Subtitle 1A.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Video lottery facility" includes:
the permitted number of video lottery terminals;
associated food and beverage operations;
associated live entertainment and dancing; and
associated parking facilities located on adjacent lots.

para.heading: Vocational school.
para.text: See "Educational facility: Commercial-vocational".

para.heading: Warehouse.
para.text: "Warehouse" means a facility for the storage and distribution of products, supplies, and equipment.

para.heading: Water-dependent facilities.
para.text: "Water-dependent facilities", as it applies to the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, has the meaning stated in § 7-402 {"CBCA Overlay: Definitions"} of this Code.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Waterfreight terminal" means a facility used for waterborne commodities.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Waterfreight terminal" includes docks, piers, wharves, storage sheds, and rail and truck facilities that service or relate to, a waterfreight terminal.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Wholesale goods establishment" means a facility primarily engaged in:
selling or distributing merchandise to retailers, to industrial, commercial, institutional, or professional business users, or to other wholesalers; or
acting as an agent or broker and buying merchandise for, or selling merchandise to, businesses of the sort listed.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Wholesale goods establishment" includes the following accessory uses:
a showroom for the display of items stored on-site; and
retail sales to the public.

para.heading: Yard (Required).
para.text: "Yard", when used with respect to required yards, means the space between a building and the adjoining lot lines that, except as otherwise permitted by this Code, is unoccupied, open, and unobstructed by any part of a structure from the ground to the sky.

para.heading: Yard: Corner-side (Required).
para.text: "Yard: Corner-side", when used with respect to required yards, means the yard that extends along the corner-side lot line between the front yard and the rear lot line for the required minimum depth, as specified for the district in which the lot is located, measured perpendicular to the corner-side lot line.

para.heading: Yard: Front (Required).
para.text: "Yard: Front", when used with respect to required yards, means the yard that extends the full width of the lot between side lot lines for the required minimum depth, as specified by the zoning district in which the lot is located, measured perpendicular to the front lot line.

para.heading: Yard: Interior-side (Required).
para.text: "Yard: Interior-side", when used with respect to required yards, means the yard that extends along an interior-side lot line, between the front and rear yards, for the required minimum depth, as specified for the district in which the lot is located, measured perpendicular to the interior-side lot line.

para.heading: Yard: Rear (Required).
para.text: "Yard: Rear", when used with respect to required yards, means the yard that extends between the side lot lines for the required minimum depth, as specified by the zoning district in which the lot is located, measured perpendicular to the rear lot line.

para.heading: Zoning Administrator; Administrator.
para.text: "Zoning Administrator" or "Administrator" means the executive head of the Office of Zoning Administrator, as established under § 3-201 {"Zoning Administrator"} of this Code, or the Administrator's designee.

para.heading: Zoning Board; BMZA.
para.text: "Zoning Board" or "BMZA" means the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, as established in City Charter Article VII, § 82.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Zoo" means a facility in which animals are exhibited or displayed to the public.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Zoo" includes the following accessory uses designed and intended primarily for patrons of the facility:
a gift or souvenir shop; and
a restaurant or refreshment stands.

section.heading: Purpose of Code.
section.text: This Code is intended to serve the following purposes:

para.text: to execute the powers and duties vested in the City of Baltimore by the State Land Use Article;
to promote and protect public health, welfare, and quality of life for current and future generations;
to ensure that the visions set forth in the City's Comprehensive Master Plan are implemented by land use regulations consistent with the goals set forth;
to promote the principles and standards enacted in the Baltimore City Sustainability Plan;
to protect the physical environment and public natural resources for all residents;
to preserve and enhance the value of structures, communities, and neighborhoods;
to preserve, protect, and promote the City's employment base; and
to provide oversight and planning to sustain the healthy growth of the City's employment centers.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Except as provided in § 2-202 {"Exempt utility and governmental uses"} of this subtitle, this Code applies to all land, uses, and structures within the corporate limits of Baltimore City.

No structure or land, in whole or in part, may be used or occupied, and no structure, in whole or in part, may be erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved, enlarged, or structurally altered unless it conforms to the provisions of this Code.
Conformance with the requirements of this Code does not obviate the need for other permits or licenses.

para.heading: Required conformance with Design Manual.
para.text: Failure to comply with the Baltimore City Design Manual is a violation of this Code.

para.heading: Required conformance with Landscape Manual.
para.text: Failure to comply with the Baltimore City Landscape Manual is a violation of this Code.

para.heading: Code controls over less restrictive agreements.

para.text: This Code is not intended to nullify any private agreement or covenant.
However, where this Code is more restrictive than a private agreement or covenant, this Code controls.

section.heading: Exempt utility and governmental uses.
section.text: Notwithstanding § 2-201 {"Application of Code"} of this subtitle, this Code does not apply to the following uses and structures, unless otherwise specifically provided in this Code:

para.text: overhead electric distribution cables and telephone lines;
underground utility lines and equipment;
conduits, vaults, pipeline laterals, and mains;
traffic signals and government-owned signs;
similar installations and equipment or accessories of a public utility or governmental service;
public transit shelters;
car- and bike-sharing facilities;
automobile charging stations, whether electric or solar;
any installation, structure, equipment, or accessory that is owned by a government entity and located in a public right-of-way;
any installation, structure, equipment, or accessory that is located in a public right- of-way and granted a franchise by Ordinance of the Mayor and City Council; and
any installation, structure, equipment, or accessory that is used by a government entity for internet or telecommunications and located on public property.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: In determining the applicability of this Code to structures or uses previously governed under other zoning regulations, the following rules apply.

para.heading: Preexisting unlawful structures and uses.
para.text: A structure or use that was unlawful at the time this Code became effective (June 5, 2017):
does not become lawful solely by the adoption of this Code or any amendment to it; and

even if made lawful by this Code or an amendment to it, remains unlawful to the extent that the structure or use conflicts with any of the requirements of this Code or of the Baltimore City Building, Fire, and Related Codes Article, including any failure to obtain the necessary use permit and occupancy permit.

para.heading: Preexisting permitted use reclassified as conditional.

para.text: If a preexisting permitted use is reclassified by this Code or an amendment to it as a conditional use for the Zoning District in which it is located, that use may be continued as a lawful conditional use, subject to the conditions and restrictions previously imposed on it by law or regulation.
Any subsequent change to that use must be approved in the manner of the original approval and is subject to the procedural and substantive requirements imposed by this Code on conditional uses.

para.heading: Preexisting nonconforming use reclassified as permitted or conditional.

para.text: If a preexisting nonconforming use is reclassified by this Code or an amendment to it as a permitted or conditional use for the zoning district in which it is located, that use may be continued as a lawful permitted or conditional use, as the case may be.

Any subsequent change to that use must be approved in the manner of the original approval, subject to this Code and, if a conditional use, to the procedural and substantive requirements imposed by this Code on conditional uses.

para.heading: Nonconformities – Preexisting lawful use no longer permitted or conditional..
para.text: If a preexisting lawful use is reclassified by this Code or an amendment to it so that the use is no longer a permitted or conditional use in the zoning district in which it is located, that use may be continued as a lawful nonconforming use, subject to the requirements and limitations imposed by Title 18 {"Nonconformities"} of this Code.

para.heading: Nonconformities – Preexisting lawful structures no longer conforming.
para.text: If a preexisting lawful structure does not meet all standards newly set forth by this Code or an amendment to it, that structure may be continued as a lawful nonconforming structure, subject to the requirements and limitations imposed by Title 18 {"Nonconformities"} of this Code.

para.heading: Nonconformities – Preexisting lawful lots no longer conforming.
para.text: If a preexisting lawful lot does not meet all standards newly set forth in this Code or an amendment to it, that lot may be continued as a lawful nonconforming lot, subject to the requirements and limitations imposed by Title 18 {"Nonconformities"} of this Code.

para.heading: Previously established planned unit development.
para.text: For planned unit developments established before June 5, 2017, transition rules are set forth in § 13-102 {"Transition rules"} of this Code.

para.heading: Previously issued building permits.
para.text: If a building permit for a structure was issued before June 5, 2017, or before the effective date of any relevant amendment to this Code and if substantial construction has occurred within 180 days of the issuance of that permit, the structure may be completed in accordance with the plans on the basis of which the building permit was issued.

para.heading: Previously granted variances and conditional uses.

para.text: All variances and conditional uses granted before June 5, 2017, or before the effective date of any relevant amendment to this Code remain effective, and the recipient of the variance and conditional use may proceed to develop the property in accordance with the approved plans.

However, if the recipient fails to act timely on the variance or conditional use, as required by § 5-309 {"Expiration of approval"} or § 5-407 {"Expiration of approval"} of this Code, the provisions of this Code govern and the approval is invalid.
Any subsequent change to a conditional use must be approved in the manner of the original approval and is subject to the procedures and requirements imposed by this Code on conditional uses.

An application that has been submitted and considered complete before June 5, 2017, or before the effective date of any relevant amendment to this Code is governed by the Code provisions in effect when the application was submitted.
A new application submitted after June 5, 2017, or after the effective date of any relevant amendment to this Code is governed by the Code provisions in effect when the application was submitted.

If a pending application is modified after its submittal, the Zoning Administrator must review the application to determine if the proposed modifications constitute a new application. If the Zoning Administrator determines that the modifications constitute a new application, the application must be resubmitted under the Code provisions then in effect at the time of resubmittal.

section.heading: Short Title.
section.text: This Code, together with the zoning map adopted under it, may be cited as the "Zoning Code of Baltimore City".

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The purpose of this title is to outline the specific powers and duties of the different administrative bodies and officials who implement this Code.

para.heading: Conflicts with Title 4 or Title 5.
para.text: In the case of any conflict between this title and Title 4 {"Development Reviews"} or Title 5 {"Applications and Authorizations"} of this Code, the provisions of Titles 4 and 5 control.
There is an Office of Zoning Administrator, constituted as an independent unit of the Department of Housing and Community Development.
The Zoning Administrator is the executive head of the Office.
Employees of the Office may be appointed as authorized by the Ordinance of Estimates.

para.heading: Powers and duties – In general.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator administers and enforces this Code.

para.heading: Powers and duties – Specific.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator has the following powers and duties under this Code:
to determine whether a variance is a major or minor variance (Title 5, Subtitle 3);
to grant minor variances (Title 5, Subtitle 3);
to authorize use permits (Title 5, Subtitle 7);
to provide zoning consultations (Title 5, Subtitle 8);
to issue zoning verifications (Title 5, Subtitle 9);
to inspect structures and uses of land to determine compliance with this Code and, where violations are found, initiate action to secure compliance;
to preserve all records from the administration of the zoning law since its enactment by Ordinance 31-1247;
to maintain permanent records of this Code and of all actions taken under it, including:
all maps adopted under this Code; and
all amendments to this Code and to the maps adopted under it;
the rules and regulations of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals;
applications for and approvals of conditional uses and variances; and
appeals taken under this Code;
to provide and maintain a public information service on matters arising out of this Code;

Where reasonable, necessary, and not a fundamental alteration of this Code, to provide reasonable accommodation in the application of this Code for the siting, development, and use of housing or services for an individual protected under the Federal Americans with Disabilities Act or the Federal Fair Housing Amendments Act;

to receive, file, review, maintain copies of, and forward to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals applications for conditional uses, variances, appeals, and other matters on which the Board is required to act;
to perform completeness review of applications (§ 5-202);

with the approval of the Board of Estimates, to set fees for processing applications, issuing permits and other authorizations, and performing the various other functions required or authorized by this Code; and
to perform all other functions assigned to the Zoning Administrator by this Code.

section.heading: Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.

para.heading: Board established.
para.text: There is a Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, as established in City Charter Article VII, § 82.

para.heading: Powers and duties.
para.text: In addition to the powers and duties specified in City Charter Article VII, §§ 83 through 89 and in State law, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals has the following powers and duties under this Code:
to grant major variances (Title 5, Subtitle 3);
to grant conditional use authorizations (Title 5, Subtitle 4);
to hear appeals from decisions of the Zoning Administrator;
with the approval of the Board of Estimates, to set fees for filing and hearing appeals, granting variances, and for the various other functions required or authorized by this Code;
to perform all other functions assigned to the Board by this Code;
to authorize accessory uses as long as they meet the standards for "accessory use", as defined in § 1-302(c) of this article; and
to authorize uses not otherwise listed in this Code, subject to § 1-217 of this article.

para.heading: Rules and Regulations.
para.text: Subject to Title 4 {"Administrative Procedure Act – Regulations"} of the City General Provisions Article, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may adopt rules and regulations:
for the conduct of its practices and procedures; and
as otherwise directed or authorized in this Code.

para.heading: Copies of all matters to Administrator.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must provide the Zoning Administrator with copies of all matters acted on by the Board, including:
all orders, requirements, decisions, determinations, rules, and regulations; and
all other information necessary for the proper administration and enforcement of this Code.

para.heading: Meetings.
para.text: Meetings of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals are held:
at the call of the chair; and
at any other time that the Board determines by general rule.

para.heading: Public hearings – Open to public.
para.text: All hearings of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals under this Code must be open to the public.

para.heading: Public hearings – Scheduling, notices, decision.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must:
fix a reasonable time and place for the public hearing of an application, appeal, or other matter;
give public notice of the hearing in accordance with Title 5 of this Code; and
require the applicant, appellant, or other person initiating the hearing to post the subject property with a notice of the time, place, and purpose of the hearing, as follows:
for a hearing on a variance or conditional use, as provided in § 5-602 {"BMZA – Major variances; conditional uses} of this Code; and
in all other cases, at least 21 days before the hearing.

para.heading: Public hearings – Oaths and witnesses.
para.text: The chair or acting chair of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may administer oaths and compel the attendance of witnesses.

para.heading: Public hearings – Attendance by parties.
para.text: At the hearing, any party may:
appear in person, by agent, or attorney; and
testify as to any material facts.

para.heading: Voting – Open to public.
para.text: All voting sessions of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must be open to the public.

para.heading: Voting – Number of votes.
para.text: The number of votes specified in the State Land Use Article is required for the Board to:
reverse any order, requirement, decision, or determination of the Zoning Administrator; or
decide in favor of the applicant on any matter on which it is required to pass under this Code.

para.heading: Minutes.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must keep minutes of all its proceedings, indicating:
the members present; and
on each question, how each member voted or that the member was absent or failed to vote.

annotations.annotation: By authority of Ordinance 20-431, Section 5, the Director of Legislative Reference, in consultation with the Law Department, has conformed subsection (c) to refer expressly to the requirements of the recently-enacted Administrative Procedure Act that, effective January 15, 2021, governs the proposal, adoption, and publication of administrative rules and regulations.

para.heading: Commission established.
para.text: There is a Planning Commission, as established in City Charter Article VII, §§ 70 and 71.

para.heading: Powers and duties.
para.text: In addition to the powers and duties specified in City Charter Article VII, § 72, the Planning Commission has the following powers and duties under this Code:
to make recommendations on amendments to the zoning text and maps (Title 5, Subtitle 5);
to make recommendations on planned unit developments (Title 13);
to develop and revise from time to time a Design Manual (Title 4, Subtitle 4);
to develop and revise from time to time a Landscape Manual (Title 4, Subtitle 5);
unless specifically provided for otherwise, to hear appeals from the decisions of the Director of Planning on:
site plan review (Title 4, Subtitle 2);
environmentally sensitive areas review (Title 4, Subtitle 3);
design review (Title 4, Subtitle 4); and
landscape review (Title 4, Subtitle 5; Landscape Manual); and
with the approval of the Board of Estimates, to set fees for filing and hearing appeals and for the various other functions required or authorized by this Code;
to begin the next comprehensive rezoning process by January 1, 2024, and submit a bill by June 30, 2025, and to repeat the process every 10 years; and
to perform all other functions assigned to the Commission by this Code.

para.heading: Position established.
para.text: There is a Director of Planning, as appointed under City Charter Article VII, § 73.

para.heading: Powers and duties.
para.text: In addition to the powers and duties specified in City Charter Article VII, §§ 74 through 80, the Director of Planning has the following powers and duties under this Code:
to perform the following reviews:
site plan review (Title 4, Subtitle 2);
environmentally sensitive areas review (Title 4, Subtitle 3);
design review (Title 4, Subtitle 4; Design Manual); and
landscape review (Title 4, Subtitle 5; Landscape Manual);
to review and grant administrative exceptions for design review (§ 4-409);
from time to time, to initiate a study of this Code, the Design Manual, and the Landscape Manual and report his or her recommendations to:
the City Council;
the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals;
the Housing Commissioner;
the Health Commissioner;
the Planning Commission; and
any others deemed appropriate; and
with the approval of the Board of Estimates, to set fees for site-plan, sensitive-area, design, and landscape reviews and for the various other functions required or authorized by this Code; and
to perform all other functions assigned to the Director by this Code.

section.heading: Commissioner of Housing and Community Development.
section.text: In addition to the powers and duties specified elsewhere in the City Code, the Commissioner of Housing and Community Development (who also serves as the Building Official) has the power and duty under this Code:

para.text: to issue use permits (Title 5, Subtitle 7); and
to perform all other functions assigned to the Housing Commissioner by this Code.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this title is to delineate:

para.text: which development permits require review and approval by the Director of Planning; and
the standards applicable to those reviews and approvals.

para.heading: Intent – Guidance, interagency review, and ensuring compliance.
para.text: Site plan review is intended:
to provide guidance to the applicant early in the design process;
to provide for interagency review; and

to ensure that the proposed development complies with this Code, the Subdivision Rules and Regulations, the Site Plan Review Manual, the Building, Fire and Related Codes, and other applicable guidelines and requirements.

para.heading: Intent – Safe and functional, etc., development.
para.text: The recommendations of site plan review are intended to ensure safe, functional, efficient, and orderly development with high standards of design.

para.heading: General purposes.
para.text: In general, the purpose of the site plan review process is to:
protect public health, safety, and welfare;
minimize adverse effects upon pedestrian and vehicular traffic;
ensure the design is safe, environmentally sound, aesthetically responsive, and protects properties, streets, and rights-of-way in the immediate vicinity, and the general public;
ensure compliance with the Comprehensive Master Plan and this Code; and
provide a consistent and uniform method of review.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The Planning Commission must develop and may revise from time to time a Site Plan Review Manual that sets forth standards and procedures for site plan review in accordance with this Code.

para.heading: Requisites for effectiveness.
para.text: This Manual and any revisions of it may take effect only after:
Planning Commission approval at a public session;
filing with the Department of Legislative Reference; and
posting on the City website.

section.heading: Applicability.
section.text: Site plan review is required for the following types of development applications:

para.text: new construction that involves any of the following:
any proposed development over 15,000 square feet of gross floor area;
developments with multiple structures on a single lot, excluding accessory structures; and
all multi-tenant commercial development, including mixed-use development;
subdivision of land;

additions or structural alterations to an existing structure, other than a single-family detached or semi-detached dwelling, that results in a 50% increase in gross floor area over the gross floor area of the existing structure prior to the addition or alteration;
planned unit development;
conditional use, unless the conditional use can and will be fully contained within an existing structure;
parking lot or structures containing 5 or more motor vehicle parking spaces;

any development within an environmentally sensitive area, including projects in a Floodplain District and projects within the Buffer of the Critical Area (see Subtitle 3 {"Environmentally Sensitive Areas Review"} of this title);
urban agriculture or community-managed open-space farm; and
any development within the C-5-IH Subdistrict.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Site plan approval is required before any permits may be issued for any development to which § 4-203 {"Applicability"} of this subtitle applies.

para.heading: Required for plan change; Time lapse.
para.text: Site plan approval is also required if:
no permits have been issued; and
either:
a final approved site plan has been changed; or
more than 1 year has passed since final approval.

section.heading: Submittal requirements.
section.text: Submittal requirements for site plan review are as found in:

para.text: the Site Plan Review Manual; and
for environmentally sensitive areas, in Subtitle 3 {"Environmentally Sensitive Areas Review"} of this title.

section.heading: Procedures.
section.text: The Director of Planning must review the project in accordance with the procedures found in the Site Plan Review Manual.

section.heading: Review standards.
section.text: Site plan review standards are as found in:

para.text: the Site Plan Review Manual; and
for environmentally sensitive areas, in Subtitle 3 {"Environmentally Sensitive Areas Review"} of this title.

para.heading: Appeal to Commission.
para.text: An applicant who is aggrieved by the final site plan decision of the Director of Planning may appeal that decision to the Planning Commission.

para.heading: When filed.
para.text: Appeals must be filed within 30 days of the Planning Director's final decision on the site plan.

para.heading: Hearing.
para.text: The Planning Commission must review the Director's decision at a public hearing held within 45 days of receiving the appeal.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of the environmentally sensitive areas development review process is to:

para.text: identify, prioritize, and protect environmentally sensitive areas during the initial stages of the development review process;
ensure that the disturbance, protection, and restoration of environmentally sensitive areas are in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations;
establish levels of protection for environmentally sensitive areas that vary with the priority ranking of each feature or combination of features;
guide site development so that negative impacts to the environmentally sensitive areas are avoided or minimized to the greatest extent possible;
encourage the use of innovative development techniques and provide flexibility in the planning process to protect the environment;
establish levels of protection for existing sensitive areas and institute requirements for the restoration of sensitive areas found to be prematurely destroyed or altered; and
protect the development from forces of nature.

para.heading: Adjacent lands.
para.text: In determining whether a proposed development contains environmentally sensitive areas all adjacent lands under the same ownership or control must be considered.

para.heading: Areas subject to process.
para.text: If a site plan contains any environmentally sensitive area, it is subject to the environmentally sensitive areas development review process.

section.heading: Approval prerequisite to permit.
section.text: Environmentally sensitive areas review is required before any permits may be issued for any development to which § 4-302 {"Applicability"} of this subtitle applies.

section.heading: Submittal requirements.
section.text: The presence or absence of environmentally sensitive areas must be documented on an existing conditions plan, to be submitted as part of site plan review. Existing environmentally sensitive areas must be shown on the existing conditions plan.

para.heading: Compliance with environmental regulations.
para.text: The Director of Planning must review the project for compliance with environmental regulations.

para.heading: Regulations listing.
para.text: Applicable regulations include:
Floodplains: City Code Article 7, Division I {"Floodplain Management"};
Chesapeake Bay Critical Area: Title 7, Subtitle 4, of this Code;
Forest Conservation: City Code Article 7, Division IV {"Forest and Tree Conservation"}; and
Significant Trees and Specimen Trees: Sites not required to comply with Forest Conservation regulations must protect these trees as required by the Baltimore City Landscape Manual.

para.heading: Appeal to Commission.
para.text: An applicant who is aggrieved by the final decision of the Director of Planning may appeal that decision to the Planning Commission.

para.heading: When filed.
para.text: Appeals must be filed within 30 days of the Planning Director's final decision on the environmentally sensitive areas review.

para.heading: Hearing.
para.text: The Planning Commission must review the Director's decision at a public hearing held within 45 days of receiving the appeal.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: Design review is intended to provide a procedure to ensure that certain development proposals comply with the design standards established under this Code.

section.heading: Design Manual.
section.text: The Planning Commission must develop and may revise from time to time a Design Manual that sets forth required design standards in accordance with the goals and objectives set forth in this subtitle.

section.heading: Goals.
section.text: The goals governing development of the Design Manual are:

para.text: to enhance the quality of the City's built environment, architectural character, and sense of place;
to foster economic vitality of the City's neighborhoods and commercial districts;
to enhance the overall urban design of Baltimore's neighborhoods; and
to enhance the quality of life of City residents with development that is sensitive to its context and adjacencies in the public realm.

section.heading: Objectives.
section.text: The objectives governing development of the Design Manual are:

para.text: to provide clear guidance for the design of residential, commercial, and mixed use development throughout the City;
to facilitate the process for design review and approval of structures within the City's development review process;
to ensure that the public realm is as thoroughly considered and articulated as principal structures;
to articulate spatial relationships, provide image, develop sense of place, and improve the aesthetics of the built environment; and
to provide flexibility and encourage creative solutions to meet the intents and purposes of the Design Manual.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, design review is required for the following types of development:
new construction of dwellings, excluding additions;
new construction of rowhouses;
upper floor additions and roof decks on existing rowhouses;
deck, porch, and balcony additions on street-front facades;
when exterior modifications are proposed for residential conversions in the R-7, R-8, R-9, and R-10 Districts;
the establishment of a non-residential use within the R-MU Overlay District;
all new construction and additions in the C-5 District;
all substantial modifications of the facade of a structure in the C-5 District;
planned unit development;
any sign that is conditional on Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals approval, but without regard to its copy or message;
any painted/mural sign, but without regard to its copy or message;
any sign over 100 square feet in area;
any electronic sign, freestanding sign, or roof sign, but without regard to its copy or message;
any freestanding sign in the C-5 or PC District, and any banner sign, projecting sign, or
wall sign above the ground floor in the C-5 or PC District, but without regard to its copy
or message;
any Signage Plan and any sign, but without regard to its copy or message, within an Area of Special Sign Control; and
any new construction that involves:
a proposed development over 15,000 square feet;
a multi-tenant commercial development, including mixed-use development;
alteration to a street-front facade in a C-1 District; or
construction in a TOD District or in the W Overlay District.

para.heading: Exception.
para.text: Design review is not required for development projects that are subject to review by the Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation.

section.heading: Approval prerequisite to permit.
section.text: Design review approval is required before any permits may be issued for any development to which § 4-405{"Applicability"} of this subtitle applies.

section.heading: Submittal requirements.
section.text: Submittal requirements for design review are:

para.text: as provided in § 5-201 {"Filing"} of this Code; and
as required by the Director of Planning.

para.heading: Director to review.
para.text: Once it is determined that an application is subject to design review, the Director of Planning must review the project for compliance with the design standards of this Code.
Design review must be completed within 15 days of receipt of a complete application.

If, in the Director's judgment, the application does not contain sufficient information to complete design review, the Director of Planning may request additional information from the applicant. In that event, the 15-day period will be suspended pending receipt of all requested information. A decision must be rendered within 15 days of receipt of the additional information.

This Code recognizes that the design standards cannot address every anticipated architectural design element of a development. Accordingly, an administrative exception to the design standards of the district may be requested during the design review process.
This administrative exception allows the Director of Planning to approve exceptions to the design standards within each of the districts.

The Director of Planning may approve an administrative exception in cases where the proposed architectural design of a structure meets the intent of the design review provisions but fails to meet 1 or more specific design standards.
The Director of Planning may not approve any administrative or other exception for any of the use, bulk, or yard standards of the zoning district.

para.heading: Standard for exceptions.
para.text: In order to approve an administrative exception, the Director of Planning must find that:
the administrative exception is generally compatible with the intent of the design standards and the area of the development; and

the design integrity and details of the building are acceptable within the context of a specific site and need not be achieved through a strict response to the details of the design standards contained in this Code.

para.heading: Appeal to Commission.
para.text: An applicant who is aggrieved by the final design review decision of the Director of Planning may appeal that decision to the Planning Commission.

para.heading: When filed.
para.text: Appeals must be filed within 30 days of the Planning Director's final decision on the design review.

para.heading: Hearing.
para.text: The Planning Commission must review the decision at a public hearing held within 45 days of receiving the appeal.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: Landscape review is intended to provide a procedure to ensure that certain development proposals comply with landscaping and screening standards of this Code.

section.heading: Landscape Manual.
section.text: The Planning Commission must develop and may revise from time to time a Landscape Manual that sets forth the required design, review, approval, installation, and maintenance of landscape in accordance with the goals and objectives set forth in this subtitle.

section.heading: Goals.
section.text: The goals governing development of the Landscape Manual are:

para.text: to improve and increase the City's environmental quality and green infrastructure network;
to preserve and enhance the City's character and sense of place;
to foster the economic vitality of the City's neighborhoods and commercial districts;
to provide a clear process for the design, review, and approval of landscape plans within the City's development review process; and
to promote the long-term health and maintenance of the City's landscape and tree canopy.

section.heading: Objectives – Environmental.
section.text: The environmental objectives governing development of the Landscape Manual are:

para.text: to foster environmentally sensitive site design that preserves natural vegetation and landforms when appropriate; and
to complement the built environment through planting that:
improves water quality and reduces stormwater run-off;
reduces soil erosion;
increases the City's tree canopy;
promotes biodiversity; and
helps to mitigate the urban heat island effect.

section.heading: Objectives – Character and sense of place.
section.text: The character-and-sense-of-place objectives governing development of the Landscape Manual are:

para.text: to articulate spatial relationships, provide image, develop sense of place, and improve the aesthetics of the built environment;
to enhance the quality of life of residents through planting that provides comfortable outdoor spaces for people to occupy;
to create pedestrian and bicycle-friendly environments; and
to provide visual screens, buffers, and shade that:
diminish undesirable views;
reduce glare, noise, and heat; and
mitigate the impacts of intensive uses.

section.heading: Objectives – Economic.
section.text: The economic objectives governing development of the Landscape Manual are:

para.text: to provide landscape design that is functional, cost effective, and sound; and
to create environments that are safe for residents and visitors and deterrents to potential criminals.

section.heading: Objectives – Landscape installation and maintenance.
section.text: The landscape-installation-and-maintenance objectives governing development of the Landscape Manual are

para.text: to ensure that landscape is installed and maintained in conformance with approved landscape plans;
to ensure that landscape is installed and maintained in a manner that will promote the proper health, function, and appearance of the landscape; and
to encourage the use of sustainable landscape construction and maintenance techniques that support the goals established by the Baltimore Sustainability Plan.

section.heading: Review process.
section.text: The Landscape Manual must provide for a review process that:

para.text: integrates the preparation, review, and approval of landscape plans into the City process for development review and approval;
coordinates landscape requirements with related regulations, including those for forest conservation, stormwater management, green building standards, and the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area; and
allows flexibility and encourages creative solutions to meet the goals and objectives of the Landscape Manual.

section.heading: Applicability.
section.text: Landscape review is required for the types of development specified in the Landscape Manual.

section.heading: Approval prerequisite to permit.
section.text: Landscape review approval is required before any permits may be issued for any development to which § 4-509 {"Applicability"} of this subtitle applies.

section.heading: Submittal requirements.
section.text: Submittal requirements for landscape review are as found in the Landscape Manual.

section.heading: Procedures.
section.text: The Director of Planning must review the project in accordance with the procedures found in the Landscape Manual.

section.heading: Review standards.
section.text: Landscape review standards are as found in the Landscape Manual.

para.heading: Appeal to Commission.
para.text: An applicant who is aggrieved by the final landscape review decision of the Director of Planning may appeal that decision to the Planning Commission.

para.heading: When filed.
para.text: Appeals must be filed within 30 days of the Planning Director's final decision on the landscape review.

para.heading: Hearing.
para.text: The Planning Commission must review the decision at a public hearing held within 45 days of receiving the appeal.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this title is to set out the general regulations governing zoning applications, variances, conditional uses, text and map amendments, notices, use permits, interpretations, and verifications.

para.heading: Introduction by ordinance.
para.text: A member of the City Council may introduce a proposed ordinance to expressly approve, authorize, or amend:
a major variance;
a conditional use;
a text amendment;
a map amendment;
an educational campus master plan;
a hospital general development plan;
an area of special sign control; or
a planned unit development.
Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this section, a person must file an application under this subsection to request:
a minor variance;
a major variance that, at the time of filing, is not the subject of legislation before the City Council;
a conditional use that, at the time of filing, is not the subject of legislation before the City Council;
a use permit;
a zoning appeal; and
a zoning consultation.
An application for a variance, conditional use, use permit, or zoning appeal must be filed by:
the owner of property to which the application applies; or
a person expressly authorized by the owner in writing.
An application for a zoning interpretation must be filed by:
an owner of any property in the City;
a person expressly authorized by a property owner in writing; or
any City Councilmember or other official of City government.
An application for a conditional use, conditional sign, or appeal from the Zoning Administrator must be filed with BMZA. All other applications must be filed with the Zoning Administrator
An application must be:
on the form provided by the City; and
filed with the number of copies that the instructions specify.

The application must include the information, plans, and data specified by the City's application requirements and sufficient to determine whether the application conforms with the requirements of this Code.
All plans must be at a scale sufficient to permit a clear and precise understanding of the proposal.

para.heading: Referral to DoT.
para.text: Within 15 business days of receiving a completed application, the Zoning Administrator or the BMZA, as the case might be, must refer the application and all accompanying documents to the Director of Transportation, if:
traffic-mitigation requirements for the proposed structure or use have not already been complied with in accordance with this Code or the City Building, Fire, and Related Codes Article; and
the proposed structure or use:
is in a Traffic-Mitigation Zone designated in Building Code § 3805 {"Traffic-Mitigation Zones"} and involves 10 or more dwelling units;
involves 15,000 sq. ft. or more of gross floor area; or
involves 50 or more dwelling units.

para.heading: Mitigation required.
para.text: A Traffic-Impact Study or the payment of a Traffic-Mitigation Fee is required if any 1 of the criteria specified in Building Code § 3802 {"Scope of Chapter"} applies.

para.heading: Procedures and conduct.
para.text: The Director of Transportation must review the application as provided in Building Code 3802 {"Scope of Chapter"}.

para.heading: Mitigation procedure.
para.text: If the Director of Transportation informs the applicant that traffic mitigation is required under Building Code Chapter 38 {"Traffic Impact and Mitigation"}, the applicant must comply with the applicable procedures and requirements of that chapter.
Applications for a conditional use, variance, or design review must be accompanied by a site plan.
The site plan must:
be drawn to scale and fully dimensioned;
indicate the lot and block, or the relevant portions of them;
show the ground area, height, and bulk of the structure, and the location of the structure in relation to the lot lines;
indicate the use to be made of the structure or land; and
include any other information that the Zoning Administrator requires for the proper administration and enforcement of this Code.
The Zoning Administrator or the Executive Director of the BMZA, as the case might be, must examine all applications within 10 days after filing.
An application is not considered complete unless, among all other requirements, all fees are paid when due.

After an application is determined to be complete, any change made by the applicant to the application must be submitted to the Zoning Administrator and the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals no later than 30 days before the date scheduled for the hearing to be held under this title.
At the Board's discretion, minor changes to the application may be made on the record at the hearing.

section.heading: Required fees.
section.text: Every application must be accompanied by the required filing fee.

section.heading: Withdrawal of application.
section.text: An applicant has the right to withdraw an application at any time before a decision is made on the application by the appropriate body. There will be no refund of fees. Requests for withdrawal must be in writing by the applicant.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Within 1 year after an application for a variance or a conditional use has been denied, the same application for the same property may not be reviewed or heard unless substantial new evidence is available.

If a zoning application is resubmitted for the same property within the 1-year period, the subsequent application must include a detailed description of how the application is a substantially different request or how substantial new evidence justifies its consideration.

The Zoning Administrator must determine whether the subsequent application is a substantially different request or presents substantial new evidence that justifies its consideration. If the Zoning Administrator finds that the application is not appropriate for resubmittal, the Zoning Administrator must summarily, and without need for a hearing, deny the request.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The purpose of the variance procedure is to afford a property owner relief from certain regulations of the Zoning Code when unnecessary hardship or practical difficulty exists.

para.heading: Application.
para.text: The variance procedure applies only to changes in bulk and yard regulations and to changes in signage, parking, and loading requirements. It does not apply to changes in the uses, the maximum quantity of signs, the location requirements of signs, or the types of signs allowed within a zoning district.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: This Code allows for 2 types of variances that may be granted under this subtitle, minor variances and major variances.
Minor variances comprise the following specified variances:
a reduction in lot width by no more than 10% of the applicable minimum lot width requirements;
a reduction in required yards and setbacks by no more than 10% or 2 feet, whichever is less;
a reduction in the number of off-street parking spaces by no more than 10% of the applicable minimum requirements;
a reduction in the required alley width for access to off-street parking; and
a variance to bulk or yard regulations if:
the parcel of land is improved with a nonconforming structure that has been in existence for at least 50 years;
the variance would not permit more than a 10% cumulative increase in the bulk and density of a structure that has been in existence for 50 or more years; and
in the opinion of the Zoning Administrator, the application complies with all applicable approval criteria for variances.
The Zoning Administrator may grant minor variances from the regulations of this Code.
Any variance not identified in subsection (b) of this section as a minor variance is a major variance.
Unless legislation has been introduced to approve a variance by ordinance, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may grant or deny any application for a major variance.

para.heading: Determinations by Zoning Administrator.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator or the Administrator's designee must determine:
whether the application is for a minor variance or a major variance; and
which City agencies and officials, if any, should be asked to review the application and submit written reports and recommendations on it.
The Zoning Administrator or designee must inform the applicant of the determination made under subsection (a)(1) of this section.
If the Zoning Administrator or designee determines the application is for a major variance, the Zoning Administrator or designee must inform the applicant that:
a major variance can be granted by ordinance or by the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals;
the applicant may request the City Council to introduce an ordinance to grant the major variance;
in the absence of legislation to approve a major variance by ordinance, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may grant or deny the major variance; and
the applicant may appeal the decision of the Zoning Administrator and the appeal must be filed within 30 days of the Zoning Administrator's decision.
The Zoning Administrator or designee must forward an application determined to be a major variance to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.

para.heading: Review standards; Notice.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator or the Administrator's designee must review and evaluate the application pursuant to the standards in § 5-308 {"Approval standards"} of this subtitle. Public notice of the application must be posted in accordance with Title 5, Subtitle 6 {"Notices"} of this Code.

para.heading: Resubmission on objection.
para.text: If written objection to the minor variance is received before the end of the required posting period, the application must be resubmitted to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals as a major variance, subject to the application, notice, and public hearing requirements applicable to major variances.

para.heading: Decision by Administrator.
para.text: If no written objection is timely received, the Zoning Administrator must render a written decision on the application within 30 days of the end of the required posting period and either approve, approve with qualifications, or deny the application.

para.heading: Appeal to BMZA.
para.text: The applicant may appeal the Zoning Administrator's decision to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals. The appeal must be filed within 30 days of the Zoning Administrator's decision.

para.heading: Review standards.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or the City Council, as the case may be, must evaluate the request for a variance, based on the evidence presented at a public hearing, in accordance with the standards in § 5-308 {"Approval standards"} of this subtitle.
The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must consider a proposed major variance in a public hearing.
Notice of the public hearing must be given in accordance with Title 5, Subtitle 6 {"Notices"} of this Code.
Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, the hearing must be concluded no more than 90 days from the Board's receipt of the completed application.

If, in the judgment of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, the application does not contain sufficient information to enable the Board to properly discharge its responsibilities, the Board may request additional information from the applicant or from City agencies or officials.
In that event, the 90-day period will be suspended or the public hearing continued pending receipt of all requested information.
The applicant may also waive this time limit by requesting a postponement from the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.
The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must render its written decision, approving, approving with conditions, or denying the application, within 30 days of the close of the public hearing.
The Board may extend this period for up to an additional 60 days for good cause on a majority vote of the Board at a publicly scheduled meeting.
All actions and other procedures taken under this subsection must immediately cease if:
the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals has not rendered a written decision under this subsection; and
the City Council has referred to the Board a bill to approve the variance by ordinance.
On this cessation of procedures, the application is deemed to be voluntarily withdrawn by the applicant.
Legislative limitation.
No legislation may be introduced to approve a major variance after the Board of Zoning Appeals has rendered a written decision on an application involving the same subject matter.

para.heading: Criteria for imposing.
para.text: Before approving any variance, the Zoning Administrator, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, or the City Council, as the case may be, may impose on the establishment, location, construction, maintenance, or operation of the variance, any condition, restriction, or limitation that it considers necessary or desirable to:
reduce or minimize the effect of the variance on other properties in the neighborhood;
secure compliance with the standards and requirements of this Code; and
better carry out the intent and purpose of this subtitle.

para.heading: Assurances of compliance.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, or the City Council, as the case may be, may require whatever evidence and guarantees considered necessary to assure that the conditions, restrictions, and limitations imposed will be met and complied with.

para.heading: Failure to comply is a violation of Code.
para.text: Failure to comply with any condition, restriction, or limitation imposed under this section constitutes a violation of this Code.

section.heading: Variance less than requested.
section.text: A variance less than that requested may be granted by the Zoning Administrator, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, or the City Council, as the case may be, if the record supports the applicant's right to some relief, but not to the entire relief requested.

para.heading: Required finding of unnecessary hardship or practical difficulty.
para.text: In order to grant a variance, the Zoning Administrator, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, or the City Council, as the case may be, must find that, because of the particular physical surroundings, shape, or topographical conditions of the specific structure or land involved, an unnecessary hardship or practical difficulty, as distinguished from a mere inconvenience, would result if the strict letter of the applicable requirement were carried out.

para.heading: Other required findings.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, or the City Council, as the case may be, must also find that:
the conditions on which the application is based are unique to the property for which the variance is sought and are not generally applicable to other property within the same zoning classification;
the unnecessary hardship or practical difficulty is caused by this Code and has not been created by the intentional action or inaction of any person who has a present interest in the property;
the purpose of the variance is not based exclusively on a desire to increase the value or income potential of the property;
the variance will not:
be injurious to the use and enjoyment of other property in the immediate vicinity; or
substantially diminish and impair property values in the neighborhood;
the variance is in harmony with the purpose and intent of this Code;
the variance is not precluded by and will not adversely affect:
any Urban Renewal Plan;
the City's Comprehensive Master Plan; or
any Historical and Architectural Preservation District; and
the variance will not otherwise:
be detrimental to or endanger the public health, safety, or welfare; or
be in any way contrary to the public interest.

para.heading: Exercise within year required.
para.text: A variance lapses and becomes void 1 year from the date of its final approval, unless substantial construction has occurred within that year.

para.heading: Extension by BMZA.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may grant an extension of this period, for both minor and major variances, on written application and for good cause shown, without notice or hearing.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Neither the Zoning Administrator nor the Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may process any application for variance if the subject property has any outstanding notices of violation, fines, or fees that are either unresolved or unpaid.

para.heading: Exception.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator or the Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may process the application for variance if the variance applied for is required to resolve an outstanding notice of violation, fine, or fee that is either unresolved or unpaid.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: This Code is based on the division of the City into districts, in which the uses of land and structures and the bulk and location of structures in relation to the land are substantially uniform. Certain uses exist, however, that, because of their unique characteristics, cannot properly be classified in any particular district without consideration, in each case, of the impact of those uses on neighboring land and of the public need for the particular use at the particular location. These uses, referred to as conditional uses, may only be approved as specified in this subtitle.

para.heading: Bulk standards.
para.text: In certain districts, bulk standards are allowed additional intensity by conditional use approval. The conditional use in these situations is interpreted as allowing the use within the structure to be more intense than would be allowed under permitted district standards.

para.heading: Signs.
para.text: In certain districts some sign types are allowed by conditional approval. The conditional approval in this situation is interpreted as allowing the sign type within a lot to be more intense that would otherwise be allowed in that district because of possible broader impact to the surrounding area.

para.heading: Section applicable to CB approvals.
para.text: This section applies to applications for conditional uses that require approval by the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.

para.heading: Referral to BMZA for action.
para.text: Once the Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals determines that an application for conditional-use approval by the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals is complete, the Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must forward the application to the Board for its consideration and action on the application.

para.heading: Referral to Planning Director, others for recommendation.
para.text: The Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must also refer the completed application to the following, for their submission within 15 days of the referral, of written reports and recommendations to the Board:
the Department of Planning; and

any other City agencies and officials that the Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals determines should be asked to review the application and submit written reports and recommendations on it.

para.heading: Review standards.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or the City Council, as the case may be, must evaluate the request for a conditional use, based on the evidence presented at the public hearing, in accordance with the standards in § 5-406 {"Approval standards"} of this subtitle.
The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must consider a proposed conditional use and conditional sign in a public hearing.
Notice of the public hearing must be given in accordance with Title 5, Subtitle 6 {"Notices"} of this Code.
Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, the hearing must be concluded no more than 90 days from the Board's receipt of the completed application.

If the Department of Planning or other City agency or official fails to timely submit its written report and recommendations, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may proceed without that report and recommendations.

If, in the judgment of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, the application does not contain sufficient information to enable the Board to properly discharge its responsibilities, the Board may request additional information from the applicant or from City agencies or officials.
In that event, the 90-day period will be suspended or the public hearing continued pending receipt of all requested information.
The applicant may also waive this time limit by requesting a postponement from the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.
The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must render its written decision, approving, approving with conditions, or denying the application within 30 days of the close of the public hearing.
The Board may extend this period for up to an additional 60 days for good cause on a majority vote of the Board at a publicly scheduled meeting.

para.heading: Imposition authorized.
para.text: Before approving any conditional use or sign, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or the City Council, as the case may be, may impose on the establishment, location, construction, maintenance, or operation of the conditional use or sign any condition, restriction, or limitation that it considers necessary for the protection of the public interest.

para.heading: Criteria for imposing.
para.text: Any condition imposed under this subsection must be reasonably related and roughly proportional to the expected impact of the conditional use.

para.heading: Failure to comply is a violation of Code.
para.text: Failure to comply with any condition, restriction, or limitation imposed under this subtitle:
constitutes a violation of this Code; and
in addition to any other civil or criminal remedy or enforcement procedure, is grounds for modification, suspension, or revocation of the conditional use.

para.heading: Evaluation criteria.
para.text: As a guide to its decision on the facts of each case, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must consider the following, where appropriate:
the nature of the proposed site, including its size and shape and the proposed size, shape, and arrangement of structures;
the resulting traffic patterns and adequacy of proposed off-street parking and loading;
the nature of the surrounding area and the extent to which the proposed use might impair its present and future development;
the proximity of dwellings, churches, schools, public structures, and other places of public gathering;
accessibility of the premises for emergency vehicles;
accessibility of light and air to the premises and to the property in the vicinity;
the type and location of adequate utilities, access roads, drainage, and other necessary facilities that have been or will be provided;
the preservation of cultural and historic landmarks and structures;
the character of the neighborhood;
the provisions of the City's Comprehensive Master Plan;
the provisions of any applicable Urban Renewal Plan;
all applicable standards and requirements of this Code;
the intent and purpose of this Code; and
any other matters considered to be in the interest of the general welfare.

para.heading: Limited criteria for denying.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or the City Council, may not approve a conditional use or sign unless, after public notice and hearing and on consideration of the standards required by this subtitle, the Board or Council finds that:
the establishment, location, construction, maintenance, or operation of the conditional use or sign would not be detrimental to or endanger the public health, safety, or welfare;
the use or sign would not be precluded by any other law, including an applicable Urban Renewal Plan;
the authorization would not be contrary to the public interest; and
the authorization would be in harmony with the purpose and intent of this Code.

para.heading: Exercise within year required.
para.text: A conditional use and a conditional sign approval lapses and becomes void 1 year from the date of its final approval unless, within that year:
a use permit under this Code and an occupancy permit under the Baltimore City Building Code have been obtained for that use;
the erection or alteration of a structure for that use has lawfully begun;
the use has lawfully begun; or
a building permit under this Code and any other applicable Codes has been obtained for the sign.

para.heading: Extension by BMZA.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may grant an extension of this period on written application and for good cause shown, without notice or hearing.

section.heading: Discontinued conditional use or conditional sign.

para.heading: Discontinued conditional use.
para.text: If any conditional use is discontinued for a continuous period of 2 years or more, the conditional use approval automatically lapses and is void. A new application and authorization is required before the conditional use may be re-established.

para.heading: Discontinued conditional sign.
para.text: If a conditional sign is removed in its entirety from the building or structure for which it was approved for a continuous period of 1 year or more, the conditional approval automatically lapses and is void. A new application is required before the conditional approval may be re-established.
