para.heading: Attempted resolution.
para.text: Whenever the Zoning Administrator learns of a violation of a condition, restriction, or limitation imposed under this subtitle, the Zoning Administrator must attempt to resolve the violation informally and promptly.
If the Zoning Administrator is unable to resolve the violation, the Zoning Administrator must issue a notice of proposed revocation to:
the owners of record of the property, as shown on the tax records of Baltimore City;
the persons to whom the conditional use approval was granted or the current operator;
the owners of record of the properties immediately adjacent to the property; and
the community, neighborhood, or improvement association listed with the Department of Planning for the area in which the property lies.
A copy of the notice must be provided to the Department of Planning.

para.heading: Contents of notice.
para.text: The notice must:
specify the nature of the violation; and

warn the recipient that, unless the violation is corrected within 30 days, or such other time as is specified in the notice, the matter will be referred to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals for potential modification, suspension, or revocation of the conditional use or sign.

para.heading: How notice served.
para.text: All notices must be served by 1 of the methods specified in § 19-207 {"Violation notice: Service"} of this Code.

If the violation is not corrected within the time specified, the Zoning Administrator must forward the record of this matter to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals and request the Board to schedule a hearing.
On receipt of the request, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must promptly schedule the matter for a hearing, to be held as soon as practicable.

If, after notice to the parties and an opportunity to be heard, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals finds that a condition, restriction, or limitation imposed under this subtitle has been violated, the Board may take any 1 or combination of the following actions:
revoke the conditional use or sign;
suspend the conditional use or sign approval subject to completion of corrective action or other condition set by the Board; or
affirm the conditional use or sign, subject to a schedule for corrective action, with provision for automatic termination if the schedule is not met.
The Board's findings must be specifically documented in the record.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Neither the Zoning Administrator nor the Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may process any application for a conditional use or sign if the subject property has any outstanding notices of violation, fines, or fees that are either unresolved or unpaid.

para.heading: Exception.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator or the Executive Director of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may process the application for a conditional use or, sign if the conditional use or sign applied for is required to resolve an outstanding notice of violation, fine, or fee that is either unresolved or unpaid.

section.heading: "Legislative authorization" defined.
section.text: In this Code, "legislative authorization" means any ordinance that:

para.text: amends the text of this Code, except as provided in § 5-502 {"Exception for corrective bills"} of this subtitle; or
approves, authorizes, or amends a prior approval or authorization relating to 1 or more specific properties, including:
a variance;
a conditional use;
a map amendment;
an educational campus master plan;
a hospital general development plan;
an area of special sign control; and
a planned unit development.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: This subtitle applies to all legislative authorizations created under authority of this Code.

para.heading: Exception for corrective bills.
para.text: This subtitle does not apply to any text amendment that:
consists only of a change in punctuation, grammar, or spelling; and
does not in any way alter the substance of this Code.

section.heading: Referrals.
section.text: Once a bill proposing a legislative authorization has been introduced, the City Council must refer the bill to the following for their written reports and recommendations:

para.text: the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals;
the Planning Commission;
the Department of Transportation; and
any other agencies that the City Council President specifies.

para.heading: Public hearing.
para.text: The Planning Commission must consider the referred bill in a public hearing. Notice of the public hearing must be given in accordance with Title 5, Subtitle 6 {"Notices"} of this Code. Except as provided in subsection (e)(2) of this section, the hearing must be concluded no more than 60 days from the Commission's receipt of the referred bill.

para.heading: Review standards.
para.text: The Planning Commission must evaluate the bill in accordance with the standards in § 5-508 {"Approval standards"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Written recommendations – Required.
para.text: Within 15 days of the close of the public hearing, the Planning Commission must:
issue its written report and recommendations; and
forward its report and recommendations, together with all agency reports and recommendations received, to the applicant and to the City Council's Executive Secretary.
For a text amendment, the Planning Commission may recommend approval, amendment, or denial of the application.
For a map amendment, the Planning Commission may recommend:
approval or denial of the application;
an alternative zoning designation than that applied for; or
the removal or addition of properties from the application.

para.heading: BMZA.
para.text: Within 30 days of the bill's introduction, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must submit its written report and recommendation to the City Council, with a copy to the Zoning Administrator.

para.heading: DoT for possible traffic mitigation.
para.text: Within 15 business days of the bill's introduction, City Council must refer the bill and all accompanying documents to the Director of Transportation for review and, if required, traffic mitigation, as provided in § 5-201(d) {"Introduction: Traffic mitigation"} of this title, if:
traffic-mitigation requirements have not already been complied with in accordance with this Code or the City Building, Fire, and Related Codes Article; and
the proposed legislative authorization:
is for property in a Traffic-Mitigation Zone designated in Building Code § 3805 {"Traffic-Mitigation Zones"} and involves 10 or more dwelling units;
involves 15,000 sq. ft. or more of gross floor area; or
involves 50 or more dwelling units.

para.heading: Other agencies.
para.text: Within 30 days of the bill's introduction, any other agencies to which the bill might have been referred must submit their written reports and recommendations to the City Council, with a copy to the Zoning Administrator.
If an agency fails to submit its written report and recommendations within the period specified by this section, the City Council may proceed without that report and recommendations.

However, the applicant may waive this time limit and consent to an extension of the reporting period by giving written notice of the waiver and consent to the President of the City Council, with copies to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, the Planning Commission, and the Zoning Administrator.
The bill must be considered at a public hearing of a committee of the City Council. Notice of the public hearing must be given in accordance with Title 5, Subtitle 6 {"Notices"} of this Code.
The committee must evaluate the bill in accordance with the standards in § 5-508 {"Approval standards"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Council options.
para.text: The City Council may approve, amend, or disapprove any legislative authorization.
Except as otherwise specified in this subsection, whenever a legislative authorization is amended:
another public hearing must be held on the bill as amended; and
the requirements of this subtitle for notice and for agency reports apply to the additional hearing.
An additional hearing is not required for:
an amendment that consists only of a change in punctuation, grammar, or spelling and does not in any way alter the substance of the ordinance;
any other amendment that does not in any way alter the substance of the ordinance;
an amendment proposed in and approved by Committee; or
an amendment to a comprehensive rezoning if, for at least 14 days before any vote is taken on the amendment, a description of the amendment:
has been provided to the Department of Legislative Reference and to the Department of Planning and by them made available for inspection and copying by the public; and
has been posted on the Department of Planning's website.

para.heading: Failure to approve.
para.text: A bill proposing a legislative authorization is considered to have failed and the application denied if the City Council fails to act finally on the bill within 12 months from the earlier of:
the date on which the last of the required agency reports and recommendations is received; and
the last day of the agency reporting period, as set by this section.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Legislative authorizations must be evaluated by the Planning Commission and the City Council in accordance with the standards set forth in this section.

para.heading: Required findings.
para.text: As required by the State Land Use Article, the City Council may approve the legislative authorization based on a finding that there was either:
a substantial change in the character of the neighborhood where the property is located; or
a mistake in the existing zoning classification.

para.heading: Required findings of fact.
para.text: In making the determination required by subsection (b)(1) of this section, the City Council must also make findings of fact that address:
population changes;
the availability of public facilities;
present and future transportation patterns;
compatibility with existing and proposed development for the area;
the recommendations of the City agencies and officials; and
the proposed amendment's consistency with the City's Comprehensive Master Plan.

para.heading: Additional standards – General.
para.text: Additional standards that must be considered for map amendments are:
existing uses of property within the general area of the property in question;
the zoning classification of other property within the general area of the property in question;
the suitability of the property in question for the uses permitted under its existing zoning classification; and

the trend of development, if any, in the general area of the property in question, including changes, if any, that have taken place since the property in question was placed in its present zoning classification.

para.heading: Additional standards – Rezoning from MI District.

para.text: To rezone land from the Maritime Industrial ("MI") District to any other zoning district, the Planning Commission must find that the proposed amendment:
is consistent with the most current Baltimore City Comprehensive Master Plan;
sustains or enhances transportation access into and out of the Port of Baltimore;
ensures the long-term preservation of the deep water assets of the Port of Baltimore for maritime industrial use;
protects maritime industrial land uses from the intrusion of non- industrial uses;
sustains or enhances the current and future maritime industrial economic development growth in the District;
establishes an adequate physical separation that will buffer non-industrial land uses from maritime industrial uses; and
adheres with federal and state laws regarding homeland security, generally, and port safety, specifically.

If an application is filed to rezone property from the Maritime Industrial District, the Director of Planning must notify the Maryland Port Administration and any adjacent property owners of the application. At least 30 days before the Planning Commission hearings on the application, the Director of Planning must seek an opinion from the Maryland Port Administration on the application of the criteria listed in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph.

para.heading: Text amendments.
para.text: Standards that must be considered for text amendments are:
the amendment's consistency with the City's Comprehensive Master Plan;
whether the amendment would promote the public health, safety, and welfare;
the amendment's consistency with the intent and general regulations of this Code;
whether the amendment would correct an error or omission, clarify existing requirements, or effect a change in policy; and
the extent to which the amendment would create nonconformities.

para.heading: Hearing required.
para.text: For a bill proposing a zoning map amendment, a zoning text amendment, or the creation, modification, or repeal of a planned unit development, the City Council committee to which the bill has been referred must conduct a hearing at which:
the parties in interest and the general public will have an opportunity to be heard; and
all agency reports will be reviewed.

para.heading: Notice of hearing required.
para.text: Notice of the hearing must be given by each of the following methods, as applicable:
by publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the City;
for the creation or modification of a planned unit development and for a zoning map amendment, other than a comprehensive rezoning:
by posting in a conspicuous place on the subject property; and
by first-class mailing of a written notice, on forms provided by the Zoning Administrator, to each person who appears on the tax records of the City as an owner of the property to be rezoned; and
for a comprehensive rezoning:
by posting in conspicuous places within and around the perimeter of the subject area or district, as the Department of Planning designates; and

by first-class mailing of a written notice, on forms provided by the Zoning Administrator, to each person who appears on the tax records of the City as an owner of property within the subject area or district.

para.heading: Contents of notice.
para.text: The notice must include:
the date, time, place, and purpose of the public hearing;
the address of the subject property or a drawing or description of the boundaries of the area affected by the proposed rezoning; and
the name of the applicant.

para.heading: Number and manner of posted notices.

para.text: For a zoning map amendment or the creation or modification of a planned unit development, the number and manner of posting is as follows:
for an individual property, at least 1 sign must be visible from each of the property's street frontages;

for a comprehensive rezoning, a change in the boundaries of a zoning district, or the creation or modification of a planned unit development, at least 2 or more signs are required, as the Department of Planning designates;
each sign must be posted at a prominent location, near the sidewalk or public right-of-way, so that it is visible to passing pedestrians and motorists;
a window-mounted sign must be mounted inside the window glass and placed so that it is clearly visible to passing pedestrians and motorists; and
each sign must be at least 3 feet by 4 feet in size.
Nothing in this subtitle prevents the voluntary posting of more notices than required by this subtitle.

para.heading: Timing of notices – In general.
para.text: The notice must be published, mailed, and, except as provided in subsection (f) of this section, posted:
at least 15 days before the public hearing; or
for a comprehensive rezoning, at least 30 days before the public hearing.

para.heading: Timing of notices – Posting for map amendment or PUDs.
para.text: For a zoning map amendment or the creation or modification of a planned unit development, the posted notice must be:
posted at least 30 days before the public hearing; and
removed within 48 hours after conclusion of the public hearing.

para.heading: Additional notice for proposed rezoning in MI District.
para.text: If an application is made to rezone any property in the MI District, the Director of Planning must notify the Maryland Port Administration and the owners of any adjacent property of the application.

para.heading: Hearing required.
para.text: For major variances and conditional uses, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or the City Council, as the case may be, must conduct a hearing at which:
the parties in interest and the general public will have an opportunity to be heard; and
all agency reports will be read.

para.heading: Notice of hearing required.
para.text: Notice of the hearing must be given by posting in a conspicuous place on the subject property.

para.heading: Contents of notice.
para.text: The notice must include:
the date, time, place, and purpose of the public hearing;
the address of the subject property or a drawing or description of the boundaries of the area affected by the proposed variance or conditional use;
the name of the applicant; and
how additional information on the matter can be obtained.

para.heading: Number and manner of posted notices.

para.text: The number and manner of posting is as follows:
for an individual property, at least 1 sign must be visible from each of the property's street frontages;
each sign must be posted at a prominent location, near the sidewalk or public right-of-way, so that it is visible to passing pedestrians and motorists;
a window-mounted sign must be mounted inside the window glass and placed so that it is clearly visible to passing pedestrians and motorists; and
each sign must be at least 3 feet by 4 feet in size.
Nothing in this subtitle prevents the voluntary posting of more notices than required by this subtitle.

para.heading: Timing of notice.
para.text: The posted notice must be:
posted at least 21 days before the public hearing; and
removed within 48 hours after conclusion of the public hearing.

para.heading: Notice of application required.
para.text: Notice of an application for a minor variance must be given by posting in a conspicuous place on the subject property.

para.heading: Contents of notice.
para.text: The notice must include:
the purpose of the application;
the address of the subject property or a drawing or description of the boundaries of the area affected by the proposed rezoning;
the name of the applicant; and
where, how, and by when any objections must be filed.

para.heading: Number and manner of posted notices.

para.text: The number and manner of posting is as follows:
for a property with more than 1 street frontage, at least 1 sign must be visible from each street frontage;
each sign must be posted at a prominent location, near the sidewalk or public right-of-way, so that it is visible to passing pedestrians and motorists;
a window-mounted sign must be mounted inside the window glass and placed so that it is clearly visible to passing pedestrians and motorists; and
each sign must be at least 3 feet by 4 feet in size.
Nothing in this subtitle prevents the voluntary posting of more notices than required by this subtitle.

para.heading: Timing of notice.
para.text: The posted notice must be:
posted at least 10 days before the Zoning Administrator makes a decision on the application; and
removed within 48 hours after a written decision is issued.

section.heading: Planning Commission consideration of site-specific projects.

para.heading: Hearing required.
para.text: For any site-specific matter, the Planning Commission must conduct a public hearing at which:
the parties in interest and general public will have an opportunity to be heard; and
staff reports and recommendations will be read.

para.heading: Notice of hearing.
para.text: In addition to any other form of notice required by law or regulation, notice of the hearing must be given by posting in conspicuous places within and around the perimeter of the subject property or area.

para.heading: Contents of notice.
para.text: The posted notice must include:
the date, time, place, and purpose of the hearing;
the address of the subject property or a drawing or description of the boundaries of the subject area;
the name and address of the applicant; and
how additional information on the matter can be obtained.

para.heading: Number and manner of posted notices.
para.text: The number of posted notices and the manner of their posting are as follows:
For a notice applicable only to an individual property, at least one sign must be visible from each of the property's street frontages.
For a notice applicable to more than one property (e.g., a modification to a Planned Unit Development), at least 2 or more signs are required, as the Department of Planning designates.
Each sign must be at least 3 feet by 4 feet in size.
Each sign must be composed of waterproof materials sufficient to ensure the sign will last the required posting period (corrugated vinyl and polyurethane banner being acceptable).

para.heading: Timing of notice.
para.text: The posted notice must be:
posted at least 10 days before the public hearing; and
removed within 48 hours after conclusion of the hearing.

para.heading: Copy of agenda to Councilmembers.
para.text: At least 4 calendar days before any meeting of the Planning Commission, the Commission must deliver to each member of the City Council, by email or in person, an agenda of all matters that the Planning Commission proposes to consider at that meeting.

para.heading: Written notice to property owners within PUD.
para.text: When applying for the creation of a new planned unit development or for a major change or repeal of a planned unit development, the applicant must provide written notification to all other owners, or their authorized agents, of property within the proposed or existing planned unit development boundaries, as the Department of Planning requires.

section.heading: Responsibility for notices.
section.text: The notices required by this subtitle must be given by and at the expense of the following:

para.text: the applicant, for applications initiated by or on behalf of a property owner; and
the Mayor and City Council, for applications initiated by the City.

section.heading: Electronic notice.
section.text: Additional electronic notice by website or email for public hearings under this Code may be provided. This notice is discretionary, and any defect in or failure to strictly adhere to an electronic notice is not a basis for declaring any legislative authorization invalid or void.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this subtitle is to set out the requirements for obtaining a use permit.

section.heading: Nature of permit.
section.text: A use permit is a document issued for a structure or land that states that the use or occupancy of the structure or land:

para.text: complies with the provisions of this Code; and
is the authorized use for that structure or land.

section.heading: Authorization and issuance.
section.text: A use permit for a structure or land is:

para.text: authorized by the Zoning Administrator; and
issued by the Housing Commissioner.

section.heading: When required.
section.text: A use permit is required before any person may:

para.text: occupy any newly-constructed structure or any addition to a previously-constructed structure;
use for any purpose any previously vacant land;
make any change in the authorized use of any land or structure; or
occupy any building that:
has been unoccupied for more than 1 year; or
is subject to an outstanding vacant building notice.

section.heading: Procedure.
section.text: The procedure for authorizing and obtaining a use permit is as determined by the Housing Commissioner.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The consultation process provided for by this subtitle recognizes that the provisions of this Code, though detailed and extensive, cannot as a practical matter address every specific zoning issue. This process is thus intended to assist in clarifying the purpose and intent of the provisions of this Code. It is not intended, however, to permit adding to or changing the essential content of this Code.

section.heading: Who may request.
section.text: The following may request a consultation with the Zoning Administrator to assist in clarifying provisions of this Code:

para.text: the owner of any property in the City;
any person expressly authorized by a property owner in writing; or
any Councilmember or other official of City government.

section.heading: Procedure.
section.text: On request under § 5-802 {"Who may request"} of this subtitle, the Zoning Administrator:

para.text: must review the request; and
may:
ask for additional information;
provide the consultation requested; and
provide a written summary of the consultation results.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Zoning consultations are meant to provide advisory information about the application of the Zoning Code. Results of a consultation are not binding on the Zoning Administrator, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, the Planning Commission, or the Mayor and City Council when addressing questions that arise under this Code.

para.heading: Disclaimer.
para.text: All written summaries of consultations must include the following statement:

"The results of any Zoning Code consultation provided under this subtitle are advisory only and are not binding on the Zoning Administrator, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, the Planning Commission, or the Mayor and City Council when making decisions on matters within the scope of their authority under the Zoning Code or any provision of federal, state, or local law or regulation."

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: A zoning verification is a document issued by the Zoning Administrator, at an applicant's request and for the applicant's own use, that states whether a property complies with the use regulations or bulk and yard regulations of the district in which it is located. It is not required by this Code.

para.text: A zoning verification may be obtained from the Zoning Administrator, on application and payment of a fee for each request.
Except as provided in paragraph (3) of this subsection, a separate application must be made for each individual lot of property.
A community-managed open-space garden or farm need only pay the fee and submit an application for verification as a single lot, as long as the lots constituting that use are contiguous.

para.heading: Required information.
para.text: Each application must contain the following information:
The block and lot number of the property;
a description or definite street location of the property;
The name and address of the present owner of the property; and
the existing and any proposed use of the property.

para.heading: Considerations.
para.text: In issuing a zoning verification, the Zoning Administrator must consider both the use specified in the application submitted for the verification and the information contained in the Zoning Administrator's official records. A zoning verification that states a property is in compliance is limited by the accuracy of the information submitted by the applicant.

section.heading: City immune from liability.
section.text: Neither the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, the Zoning Administrator, nor any of their officers, agents, or employees may be held liable to any person, under any circumstances, in connection with or resulting from the issuance of any zoning verification or in connection with or resulting from any information or statement contained in any zoning verification.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this title is to outline the different zoning districts and the zoning map, floodplain overlay maps, and flood profiles subject to this Code.

section.heading: Establishment of districts.
section.text: To carry out the purposes of this Code, the City is divided into zoning districts, as listed in this subtitle and located on the zoning map, floodplain overlay maps, and flood profiles adopted under this Code.

section.heading: Open-Space and Environmental Districts.
section.text: The Open-Space and Environmental Districts are:

tr.td: Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Overlay Zoning District

section.heading: Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Districts.
section.text: The Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Districts are:

tr.td: Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Zoning District
Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Zoning District

section.heading: Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Districts.
section.text: The Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Districts are:

tr.td: Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Zoning District
Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Zoning District
Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Zoning District
Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Zoning District
Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Zoning District
Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Zoning District

section.heading: Commercial Districts.
section.text: The Commercial Districts are:

tr.td: Neighborhood Business and Entertainment Zoning District

section.heading: Industrial Districts.
section.text: The Industrial Districts are:

section.heading: Special Purpose Districts.
section.text: The Special Purpose Districts are:

section.heading: Maps and profiles part of Code.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The zoning map, floodplain overlay maps, and flood profiles adopted under this Code are incorporated in and made a part of this Code as fully as if they were set forth and described in this Code.

para.heading: Evidence of authenticity.
para.text: As evidence of the authenticity of these maps and profiles, each is to be signed by the Mayor and by the President of the City Council.

The Zoning Administrator may convert these maps and profiles into, and maintain and periodically update them in, a geographic database or other digital format that is capable of depicting the zoning lines and designations in both electronic and printed forms.
On certification by the Director of Transportation, the maps and profiles converted to a digital format under this subsection:
are legalized for purposes of the Zoning Code of Baltimore City; and
may be taken by all public officials and others as evidence of the original maps and profiles adopted under this Code.

section.heading: Letter or letter-number designations.
section.text: The use on the zoning map of a letter or a letter-number combination to designate a district indicates that the regulations applying to that district extend throughout the whole area bounded by the district boundary lines, as determined by the provisions of § 6-303 {"Boundary line determination"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The precise location of a zoning district boundary line is determined as specified in this section.

para.heading: Along streets, alleys, streams, etc.
para.text: Where a district boundary line is shown as being within or along a street, alley, other public or private way, or an extension of any of them, or as being within or along a non-navigable stream, the boundary is the center line of that street, alley, other way, extension, or stream.

para.heading: On lot lines.
para.text: Where a district boundary line is shown as along or superimposed on a lot line, the boundary is that lot line.

para.heading: Designated distances.
para.text: Where the location of a district boundary line is indicated by a designated number of feet, that distance controls.

para.heading: Along railroad rights-of way.
para.text: Where a district boundary line is shown as being within or along a railroad right-of-way, the boundary line of that railroad right-of-way controls.

para.heading: Along navigable waters.
para.text: Where a district boundary line is shown as along a navigable waterway and is not otherwise fixed, the boundary is:
the line that coincides with the "pierhead line" (that is, the legal boundary beyond which artificial structures, such as piers, may not project); or
where no pierhead line has been established, the line that coincides with the mean low tide line.

para.heading: Reclaimed submerged land.
para.text: Unless otherwise indicated on the zoning map, submerged land that is later reclaimed is in the same district as the non-submerged premises to which the reclaimed land is contiguous.

para.heading: Others.
para.text: Where a district boundary line is shown and its location is not fixed by any of the rules of this section, its precise location is determined by scaling from fixtures, objects, or other structures shown on the zoning map.

section.heading: Property divided by zoning district line.
section.text: Where a lot is divided into 2 or more parts by a zoning district line:

para.text: for all purposes except density, each part must comply with all of the regulations applicable to its zoning classification; and
for density purposes, the lot area computation of each part may be totaled and then distributed throughout the lot, without regard to the zoning lines.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this title is to set out the use regulations, bulk and yard regulations, and other standards for:

para.text: Open-Space Zoning Districts;
Floodplain Overlay Zoning Districts; and
Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Overlay Zoning District.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The purpose of the Open-Space ("OS") Zoning District is to enhance the quality of life for City residents by permanently preserving public open space as an important public asset and critical environmental infrastructure.

para.heading: Regulatory intent.
para.text: The regulations for this district are intended to:
protect and promote public and private open space;
provide public reflective, cultural, educational, and recreational opportunities;
enhance the urban environment;
provide pedestrian and bicycle transportation connections;
encourage neighborhood investment in and stewardship of natural green spaces and native flora and fauna;
protect and enhance natural resources, including forests, habitat, and water quality; and
ensure the environmental benefits of adequate light, air, and water in City neighborhoods.

para.heading: Application.
para.text: The Open-Space District applies to public and private open space properties and cemeteries.

section.heading: Use regulations.
section.text: Only those uses of land listed in Table 7-202: Open-Space Districts – Permitted and Conditional Uses are allowed within an Open-Space Zoning District.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Table 7-203: Open-Space Districts – Bulk and Yard Regulations sets forth the applicable bulk and yard regulations for an Open-Space Zoning District.
Measurement methodologies are as set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 3 {"Measurement Methodologies"} of this Code.
Exceptions and requirements are as set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 4 {"Exceptions and Requirements"} of this Code.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The Open-Space Zoning District is also subject to the standards identified in this section.

para.heading: Accessory structures and uses.
para.text: Standards governing accessory structures and uses are as set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 5 {"Accessory Structures and Uses"} of this Code.

para.heading: Site development standards.
para.text: On-site development standards are set forth in Title 15 {"Site Development Standards"} of this Code.

para.heading: Off-Street parking and loading.
para.text: Standards governing off-street parking and loading are as set forth in Title 16 {"Off-Street Parking and Loading"} of this Code.

para.heading: Landscaping and screening.
para.text: All landscaping and screening must comply with the requirements of the Baltimore City Landscape Manual.

para.heading: Signs.
para.text: Sign standards are as set forth in Title 17 {"Signs"} of this Code.

para.heading: Temporary uses.
para.text: Standards governing temporary uses are as set forth in Title 14, Subtitle 4 {"Temporary-Use Standards"} of this Code.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: In this subtitle, the following terms have the meanings indicated.

para.heading: Floodplain.
para.text: "Floodplain" has the meaning stated in City Code Article 7 {"Natural Resources"}, § 1-2(v) {"Definitions: Floodplain"}.

para.heading: Floodplain maps.
para.text: "Floodplain maps" means the series of maps and profiles known as the Flood Insurance Rate Maps and Flood Insurance Study for the City of Baltimore, dated June 16, 2021, as prepared, revised, or amended from time to time for the Federal Emergency Management Agency, Flood Insurance Administrator in accordance with City Code Article 7, Division I {"Floodplain Management"}.

para.heading: Floodplain Overlay Zoning District; Floodplain District; Overlay District.
para.text: "Floodplain Overlay Zoning District", "Floodplain District", or "Overlay District" means all areas shown as floodplains on the floodplain maps.

section.heading: Purpose of Floodplain Overlay District.
section.text: The Floodplain ("FP") Overlay Zoning District regulates the placement and use of structures and the use of land in the floodplain, with the design towards:

para.text: protecting human life and health;
minimizing damage to public and private property;
preventing or minimizing future flood damage;
protecting the public water supply and sanitary sewage disposal systems;
preserving natural drainage systems; and
reducing financial burdens imposed on the City and its citizens.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The Floodplain Overlay Zoning District is divided into the following 6 subdistricts, each designating a measurable degree of flood hazard, as delineated on the floodplain maps.

para.heading: Floodway.
para.text: The Floodway comprises that part of the Overlay District that is described in City Code Article 7, § 2-2(b) {"Subdistricts: Floodway"}.

para.heading: Floodway Fringe.
para.text: The Floodway Fringe comprises those lands within the Overlay District that are described in City Code Article 7, § 2-2(c) {"Subdistricts: Floodway Fringe"}.

para.heading: Approximated Floodplain.
para.text: The Approximated Floodplain comprises those lands within the Overlay District that are described in City Code Article 7, § 2-2(d) {"Subdistricts: Approximated Floodplain"}.

para.heading: Coastal Floodplain.
para.text: The Coastal Floodplain comprises those lands within the Overlay District that are described in City Code Article 7, § 2-2(e) {"Subdistricts: Coastal Floodplain"}.

para.heading: Coastal High Hazard Area.
para.text: The Coastal High Hazard Area comprises those lands within the Overlay District that are described in City Code Article 7, § 2-2(f) {"Subdistricts: Coastal High Hazard Area"}.

para.heading: Flood Resilience Area.
para.text: The flood resilience area comprises those lands within the Overlay District that are described in City Code Article 7, § 2-2(g) {"Subdistricts: Flood Resilience Area"}.

para.heading: Per underlying district.
para.text: Except as otherwise specifically limited or prohibited by this section or by other applicable law (See § 7-309 of this subtitle), all uses allowed in a Floodplain Overlay Zoning District are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district.

para.heading: Conditional uses.
para.text: In addition to the general requirements of this Code governing conditional uses, a conditional use in a Floodplain Overlay District is subject to the standards and procedures contained in § 7-306 {"Variances and conditional uses"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Floodway.
para.text: The only uses allowed in the Floodway are the following recreational facilities, but not including accessory buildings:
athletic fields;
golf courses; and
parks.

para.heading: Public utility or government office.
para.text: Notwithstanding any other provision to the contrary, no public utility or government service use may be located in any floodplain if it:
might impede, retard, or change the direction of the flow of water;
will catch or collect debris carried by the water; or
is placed where the natural flow of the stream or floodwaters would carry it downstream to the damage or detriment of any public or private property in or adjacent to the floodplain.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The bulk and yard regulations applicable to properties in a Floodplain Overlay Zoning District are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district.

para.heading: Variances.
para.text: In addition to the general requirements of this Code governing variances, a variance in a Floodplain Overlay Zoning District is subject to the standards and procedures contained in § 7-306 {"Variances and conditional uses"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Standards for substantial improvements or new construction.

para.text: In addition to the other requirements of this Code governing variances and conditional uses, the additional standards specified in paragraph (2) of this subsection apply to any variance or conditional use that involves any substantial improvement or new construction in a Floodplain Overlay Zoning District.
All variances and conditional uses described in paragraph (1) of this subsection are subject to the following additional standards:
the variance or conditional use will not result in increased flood heights or additional danger to the public health, safety, or welfare;
the proposal is consistent with the need to minimize flood damage;
all necessary permits have been received from the appropriate state and federal agencies;
all public and private utilities and facilities (including sewer, water, telephone, electric, gas, etc.) are located and constructed to minimize or eliminate flood damage;
adequate drainage is provided to reduce exposure to flood hazard; and
the variance or conditional use is necessary because of extraordinary circumstances in local conditions that render the application of certain standards a severe hardship.

para.heading: Warning letters.
para.text: If the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals grants a variance or conditional use under this section, the Board must attach to its decision a warning that:
construction below the base flood level may result in increased premium rates for flood insurance; and
construction below the base flood level increases risks to life and property.

section.heading: Municipal and personal liability.
section.text: A zoning authorization for property that is near a delineated floodplain or near any other land later discovered to be a floodplain:

para.text: is not a representation, guarantee, or warranty of any kind that the property is not in a floodplain; and
may not be used to impose any liability on the City, its elected or appointed officials, or its employees.

section.heading: Other applicable laws.
section.text: The Floodplain Overlay Zoning District is also subject to the standards, limitations, and prohibitions set forth in other applicable laws governing floodplains and flood hazard areas, including:

para.text: City Code Article 7, Division I {"Floodplain Management"}; and
the City Building, Fire, and Related Codes Article.

container.heading: Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Overlay Zoning District

section.heading: Purpose of Critical Area Overlay District.
section.text: The Chesapeake Bay Critical Area ("CBCA") Overlay District is designed to foster more sensitive, consistent, and uniform development and redevelopment activity along the City's shoreline areas of the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries, so as to minimize damage to water quality and natural or established habitats for the benefit of current and future generations.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: In this subtitle, the following terms have the meanings indicated.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Buffer" means area that:
based on conditions at the time of development, is immediately landward from mean high water of tidal waterways, the edge of a bank of a tributary stream, or the edge of a tidal wetland; and
exists, or may be established in, natural vegetation to protect a stream, tidal wetland, tidal waters or terrestrial environments from human disturbance.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Buffer" includes:
an area of at least 100-feet, even if that area was previously disturbed by human activity; and
any expansion for contiguous areas, including a steep slope, hydric soil, highly erodible soil, nontidal wetland, or a Nontidal Wetland of Special State Concern as defined in COMAR 26.23.01.01.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Critical Area" means all lands and waters defined in §8-1807 of the State Natural Resources Article.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Critical Area" includes:
all waters of and lands under the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their tributaries to the head of tide;
all State and private wetlands designated under Title 16 of the State Environment Article;
all land and water areas within 1,000 feet beyond the landward boundaries of State or private wetlands and the heads of tides designated under Title 16 of the State Environment Article; and

modification to these areas through inclusions or exclusions proposed by local jurisdictions and approved by the Critical Area Commission, as specified in § 8-1807 of the State Natural Resources Article.

para.heading: Critical Area Management Program.
para.text: "Critical Area Management Program" or "CAMP" means the Baltimore City Critical Area Management Program, as adopted by Resolution or Ordinance of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore and approved by the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Commission.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Development" has the meaning stated in COMAR 27.01.01.01B(21).

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Development" includes any one or a combination of the following:
construction, reconstruction, modification, expansion, or demolition of structures;
placement of fill;
dredging;
drilling;
mining;
grading;
paving;
land excavation;
land clearing;
land improvement; or
storage of materials.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Disturb" means to alter or change land in any way.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Disturb" includes any amount of clearing, grading, or construction activity.

para.heading: Exclusions.
para.text: "Disturb" does not include gardening or maintenance of an existing grass lawn.

para.heading: Significant development.
para.text: "Significant development" means any development that would:
disturb any land in the Buffer;
disturb 10,000 or more square feet of land in the Critical Area;

result in any disturbance, caused by use, development, or destruction of vegetation, to land in an area designated under the Critical Area Management Program as a "Designated Habitat Protection Area"; or
involve an expenditure for improvements to the property equal to or greater than 50% of the assessed value of the property, as recorded in the State Department of Assessment and Taxation's database.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: "Water-dependent facilities" means land uses or structures that:
are associated with industrial, maritime, recreational, educational, or fisheries activities;
require a location within the Buffer near the shoreline; and
are dependent on the water by reason of the intrinsic nature of their operation.

para.heading: Inclusions.
para.text: "Water-dependent facilities" include:
ports;
intake and outfall structures of power plants;
industries that withdraw water from surface waters regulated by this State, requiring a Water Appropriation and Use Permit from the Maryland Department of the Environment;
marinas and other boat-docking structures;
public beaches and water-oriented recreation areas; and
fisheries.

para.heading: Exclusions.
para.text: "Water-dependent facilities" does not include private piers that are installed and maintained by riparian landowners and are not part of a subdivision that provides community piers.

section.heading: Designation of Critical Area.
section.text: The Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Act (State Natural Resources Article Title 8, Subtitle 18) requires the City to designate as its Critical Area an area that consists of, at a minimum:

para.text: all waters of and lands under the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries to the head of tide, and all State and private wetlands designated under Title 16 of the State Environment Article; and
all land and water areas within 1,000 feet beyond the landward boundaries of State or private wetlands and the heads of tides designated under Title 16 of the State Environment Article.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: State law requires the City to designate "Development Areas" within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, based generally on existing development patterns and densities.

para.heading: Types Designated.
para.text: The 2 types of Development Areas specified in the Critical Area Management Program are:
"Resource Conservation Areas"; and
"Intensely Developed Areas", which comprise 2 subareas designated as:
"Waterfront Industrial Areas"; and
"Waterfront Revitalization Areas", which include subareas designated as:
"Waterfront Industrial Areas".

para.heading: Boundaries delineated on Map.
para.text: The boundaries of the Critical Area, the Buffer, and the Development Areas are delineated on the Baltimore City CAMP Map (2020 Edition), as published and maintained by the Baltimore City Department of Planning.

para.heading: Map amendments.
para.text: In addition to the requirements of Title 5, Subtitle 5 {"Legislative Authorizations"} of this Code, any amendment to the CAMP Map must be reviewed and approved by:
the Planning Commission; and
the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Commission.

para.heading: Digital format authorized.
para.text: With the approval of the Planning Commission and the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Commission, the Department pf Planning may create, convert, or update the CAMP Map in a geographic database or other digital format that is capable of depicting the boundaries and designations in both electronic and printed forms.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The CAMP Map approved under this section:
is legalized for purposes of the Zoning Code of Baltimore City; and
may be taken by all public officials and others as evidence of the boundaries and designations adopted under this subtitle and the Baltimore City Critical Area Management Program.

para.heading: Other depictions illustrative only.
para.text: Any other representation of the Critical Area, Buffer, or Development Areas, regardless of the source of publication, are illustrative only and may not be used for determining any of the development requirements or restrictions required in this subtitle or by the Critical Area Management Program.

para.heading: Scope.
para.text: The uses prohibited by this section are in addition to those prohibited by§ 1-218 {"Uses prohibited citywide"} of this Code.

para.heading: Within Critical Area.
para.text: Except as specified in subsection (d) of this section, the following uses are prohibited within the Critical Area:

a dwelling unit or other non-water dependent structure on a pier, wharf, dock, walkway, bulkhead, breakwater, piles, or other similar structure, except as authorized under State Natural Resources Article § 8-1808.4 {"Critical Area Protection Program: Nonwater-dependent projects"};
collection, storage, handling, or disposal of hazardous or toxic materials, as defined in COMAR 11.07.01.01;
industrial landfills;
liquefied natural gas and petroleum gas terminals;
maintenance, dismantling, or storage of abandoned, unlicensed, junked, or derelict vehicles or vehicle parts;
non-water dependent uses on barges in tidal waters, except maritime museums;
non-water dependent uses on permanently moored vessels in the Inner Harbor Basin, except maritime museums;
recycling collection stations;
solid waste acceptance facilities, as defined in City Code Article 23, except for facilities approved as a conditional use under this subtitle; and
storage and handling of radioactive waste.

para.heading: Within Buffer.
para.text: Except as specified in subsection (d) of this section, the following additional uses are prohibited within the Buffer:
cement plants;
chemical plants;
sand or gravel extraction operations; and
storage facilities for nutrients – that is, elements or compounds essential as raw material for organic growth and development (for example, carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus).

para.heading: Exceptions.
para.text: The prohibitions in subsections (b) and (c) of this section do not apply if the following standards are met:
on recommendation of the Department of Planning, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals finds both that:
there is no environmentally acceptable alternative outside the Critical Area; and
the use is needed to correct an existing water quality or wastewater management problem; and

for any new use that constitutes a significant development or for any expansion of a nonconforming use, a best management practices plan that will achieve a net improvement in water quality and habitat is submitted and implemented as a requirement of the Critical Area review process.

para.heading: Water-dependent facilities prohibited.
para.text: Non-public water-dependent facilities are prohibited in Resource Conservation Areas.

para.heading: Permitted and accessory uses outside Buffer.
para.text: In a Resource Conservation Area outside the Buffer, permitted and accessory uses are:
open space;
public recreation;
natural parks;
pedestrian easements;
bike paths; and
cultural and historical sites.

para.heading: Permitted and accessory uses within Buffer.
para.text: In a Resource Conservation Area within the Buffer, permitted and accessory uses are areas for passive recreation, such as nature study and education, but service facilities for these areas must be located outside of the Buffer.

para.heading: Conditional uses outside Buffer.
para.text: In a Resource Conservation Area outside the Buffer, conditional uses are public facilities.

para.heading: Conditional uses within Buffer.
para.text: In a Resource Conservation Area within the Buffer, conditional uses are public water-dependent facilities.

section.heading: Intensely Developed Areas – Waterfront Revitalization; Shoreline Conservation.

para.heading: Permitted and accessory uses outside Buffer.
In general.
para.text: In a Waterfront Revitalization Area outside the Buffer, permitted and accessory uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited uses"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Shoreline Conservation Areas.
para.text: In a Waterfront Revitalization subarea designated a Shoreline Conservation Area, no new bulkheads are allowed within 30 feet from the mean high water line.

para.heading: Permitted and accessory uses within Buffer.
para.text: In a Waterfront Revitalization Area within the Buffer, permitted and accessory uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited Uses"} and § 7-410 {"Intensely Developed Areas – Water-dependent facilities within Buffer"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Conditional uses outside Buffer.
para.text: In a Waterfront Revitalization Area outside the Buffer, conditional uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited uses"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Conditional uses within Buffer.
para.text: In a Waterfront Revitalization Area within the Buffer, conditional uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited uses"} and § 7-410 {"Intensely Developed Areas – Water-dependent facilities within Buffer"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Permitted and accessory uses outside Buffer.
para.text: In a Waterfront Industrial Area outside the Buffer, permitted and accessory uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited uses"} of this subtitle.

para.heading: Permitted and accessory uses within Buffer.
para.text: In a Waterfront Industrial Area within the Buffer, permitted and accessory uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited Uses"} and § 7-410 {"Intensely Developed Areas – Water-dependent facilities within Buffer"} of this subtitle.

In a Waterfront Industrial Area outside the Buffer, conditional uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited uses"} of this subtitle.

Solid-waste acceptance facilities of the following types require conditional-use approval: waste-to-energy facilities, indoor-operated transfer facilities, and indoor-operated composting facilities, such as "in-vessel" composting facilities. If the use entails any significant development, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must find, as a condition of its approval, that a best management practices plan that will achieve a net improvement in water quality and habitat is submitted and implemented as a requirement of the Critical Area review process.

para.heading: Conditional uses within Buffer.
para.text: In a Waterfront Industrial Area within the Buffer, conditional uses are as otherwise provided in this Code for the underlying zoning district, subject to the provisions of § 7-406 {"Prohibited Uses"} and § 7-410 {"Intensely Developed Areas – Water-dependent facilities within Buffer"} of this subtitle.

section.heading: Intensely Developed Areas – Water-dependent facilities within Buffer.
section.text: In Intensely Developed Areas, water-dependent facilities are allowed in the Buffer only if all of the following standards are met:

para.text: the use and project meet a recognized private right or public need;
adverse effects on water quality and on fish, plant, and wildlife habitats are minimized and equivalent offsets have been made;
to the extent possible, all associated non-water-dependent uses and structures are located outside the Buffer; and
the facilities meet the requirements of the Critical Area Management Program, the Critical Area Development Manual, and the State law and regulations governing the Critical Area.

section.heading: Public utility and government services.
section.text: Notwithstanding any other provision to the contrary, every significant development of public utilities or governmental services within the Critical Area is subject to the special requirements and restrictions of the Critical Area Management Program.

section.heading: Abandoned uses.
section.text: Any use in the Critical Area Overlay District that is discontinued for 12 consecutive months:

para.text: is considered abandoned; and

may not be reestablished in the Critical Area unless, on recommendation of the Department of Planning, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals finds that the use complies with the Critical Area Management Program.

section.heading: Bulk and yard regulations.
section.text: Properties in the Critical Area Overlay District are subject to:

para.text: the bulk and yard regulations in the underlying zoning district; and
to the extent that they are more restrictive, the lot coverage limitations imposed by the Critical Area Management Program.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: In addition to the general requirements of this Code governing variances and conditional uses, a variance or conditional use in the Critical Area is subject to the standards and procedures of:
State Natural Resources Article Title 8, Subtitle 18;
COMAR Title 27;
the Critical Area Management Program; and
this section.

para.heading: Existing violations.
para.text: No conditional use or variance may be granted to authorize a then-existing violation except as authorized in State Natural Resources Article § 8-1808 {"Critical Area Protection Program: Program development..."}.

para.heading: Considerations, presumptions, and burden of proof.

para.text: In considering an application for a conditional use or variance, the Planning Department and the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must presume that the specific development activity for which a conditional use or variance is required does not conform with the general purpose and intent of State Natural Resources Article, Title 8, Subtitle 18, the general purpose and intent of COMAR Title 27, or the requirements of the Critical Area Management Program.

If the request for a conditional use or variance is based on conditions or circumstances that are the result of actions by the applicant, including the commencement of development activity before an application is filed, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may consider that fact.
An applicant has the burden of proof and the burden of persuasion to overcome the presumption of nonconformance established by paragraph (1) of this subsection.
The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must make written findings as to whether, based on competent and substantial evidence, the applicant has overcome this presumption.
With due regard for the person's experience, technical competence, and specialized knowledge, the findings may be based on evidence introduced and testimony presented by either:
the applicant.
the City or any other government agency; and
any other person considered appropriate by the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.

para.heading: Applications.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must furnish copies of all applications for a conditional use or variance to the Planning Department and the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area Commission.

para.heading: Findings – Planning Department.
para.text: The Planning Department must find both that:
special conditions or circumstances exist that are peculiar to the land or structure for which the application is made; and

a literal enforcement of the requirements of the Critical Area Management Program would result in the applicant's being denied reasonable and significant use of the entire parcel or lot for which the conditional use or variance is requested.

para.heading: Findings – Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals.
para.text: In addition, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must find that all of the following standards are met:

a literal interpretation of the Critical Area Management Program, the State Chesapeake Bay Critical Area law, or related regulations will deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties in similar areas within the Critical Area;

the granting of a conditional use or variance will not confer on the applicant any special privilege that would be denied under the Critical Area Management Program, the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area law, or related regulations to other lands or structures within the Critical Area;

the granting of a conditional use or variance will not adversely affect water quality or adversely impact fish, wildlife, or plant habitats within either the Critical Area or any other protected part of the State Chesapeake Bay Critical Area within a neighboring jurisdiction;

the granting of a conditional use or variance will be in harmony with the general spirit and intent of the Critical Area Management Program, the State Chesapeake Bay Critical Area law, and related regulations; and
the application for the conditional use or variance either:
is not based on conditions or circumstances that are the result of the applicant's own actions; or
does not arise from any condition that relates to a land or building use, whether nonconforming or otherwise allowed, on any neighboring property.
This section is enacted by authority of State Natural Resources Article § 8-1808(c)(1)(iii)14.
This section applies in addition to any other civil or criminal penalty authorized by State or City law.

para.heading: Administrator may impose.
para.text: Any person who violates a provision of this subtitle, of the Critical Area Management Program, or of any rule or regulation adopted under them, including any contractor, property owner, or other person who authorizes or who assists or participates in the violation, is subject to the imposition by the Zoning Administrator of a civil fine of up to $1,000 for each offense.

para.heading: Each day a separate offense.
para.text: Each day that a violation continues is a separate offense.

para.heading: Considerations.
para.text: In determining the amount of the penalty to be imposed under this section, the Zoning Administrator must consider the following:
the gravity of the violation;
any willfulness or negligence involved in the violation;
the environmental impact of the violation; and

the cost of restoring and mitigating the damage to the resource affected by the violation, including the cost to the State or the City for performing, supervising, or rendering assistance to the restoration and mitigation.

para.heading: Procedures.
para.text: The procedures for imposing the fine and for providing notice and an opportunity to be heard are as set forth in the Administrative Enforcement Procedures of the Critical Area Management Program.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this title is to set out the use regulations and the bulk and yard regulations for Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Districts.

para.heading: Residential development.
para.text: In the districts described in this subtitle, residential development is limited to 1 single-family dwelling unit per lot.

para.heading: Residential conversions.
para.text: In any of the districts subject to this title, the conversion of a single-family dwelling to a multi-family dwelling is prohibited.

section.heading: R-1A Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-1A Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for neighborhoods of detached dwellings located on large lots of at least 2 acres in areas of countryside character, where environmental sensitivity is required during development to preserve natural features and where transportation access is more limited.

section.heading: R-1B Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-1B Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for neighborhoods of detached dwellings located on large lots of at least 1 acre in areas of countryside character, where environmental sensitivity is required during development to preserve natural features and where transportation access is more limited.

section.heading: R-1C Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-1C Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for neighborhoods of detached dwellings located on large lots of at least 21,780 square feet in areas of established low density development.

section.heading: R-1D Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-1D Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for low density neighborhoods of detached dwellings located on lots of at least 14,520 square feet.

section.heading: R-1E Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-1E Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for neighborhoods of detached dwellings located on lots of at least 9,000 square feet.

section.heading: R-1 Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-1 Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for neighborhoods of detached dwellings located on lots of at least 7,300 square feet.

section.heading: R-2 Detached and Semi-Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-2 Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for residential neighborhoods that accommodate both detached and semi-detached dwellings located on lots of at least 5,000 square feet.

section.heading: R-3 Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-3 Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for neighborhoods of detached dwellings located on lots of at least 5,000 square feet.

section.heading: R-4 Detached and Semi-Detached Residential District.
section.text: The R-4 Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Zoning District is intended for neighborhoods that accommodate detached and semi-detached dwellings located on lots of at least 3,000 square feet.

section.heading: As listed in Table 8-301.
section.text: Only those uses of land listed in Table 8-301: Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Districts – Permitted and Conditional Uses are allowed within these zoning districts.

section.heading: In general.
section.text: Table 8-401: Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Districts – Bulk and Yard Regulations sets forth the applicable bulk and yard regulations for these zoning districts.

para.heading: Measurement methodologies.
para.text: Measurement methodologies are as set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 3 {"Measurement Methodologies"} of this Code.

para.heading: Exceptions and requirements.
para.text: Exceptions and requirements are as set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 4 {"Exceptions and Requirements"} of this Code.

section.heading: In general.
section.text: The Detached and Semi-Detached Residential Zoning Districts are also subject to the standards listed in this subtitle.

section.heading: Accessory structures and uses.
section.text: Standards governing accessory structures and uses are set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 5 {"Accessory Structures and Uses"} of this Code.

section.heading: Site development.
section.text: On-site development standards are set forth in Title 15 {"Site Development Standards"} of this Code.

section.heading: Off-street parking and loading.
section.text: Standards governing off-street parking and loading are set forth in Title 16 {"Off-Street Parking and Loading"} of this Code.

section.heading: Design standards.
section.text: All developments of the type described in § 4-405 {"Design Review: Applicability"} of this Code must comply with the applicable design standards required by the Baltimore City Design Manual.

section.heading: Landscaping and screening.
section.text: All landscaping and screening must comply with the requirements of the Baltimore City Landscape Manual.

section.heading: Signs.
section.text: Standards governing signs are set forth in Title 17 {"Signs"} of this Code.

section.heading: Temporary uses.
section.text: Standards governing temporary uses are set forth in Title 14, Subtitle 4 {"Temporary-Use Standards"} of this Code.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this title is to set out the use regulations and the bulk and yard regulations for Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Districts.

para.heading: Neighborhoods.
para.text: The R-5 Transitional Residential Zoning District is intended for those areas that facilitate a transition from primarily single-family neighborhoods to neighborhoods that contain a wider mix of housing types.

para.heading: Housing types.
para.text: The R-5 District is meant to accommodate single-family units in both detached and semi-detached dwellings, rowhouse developments, and limited low-rise multi-family garden apartment developments of a moderate density.

para.heading: Neighborhoods.
para.text: The R-6 Garden Rowhouse Residential Zoning District is intended for primarily low density rowhouse neighborhoods that reflect a naturalistic environment typified by open and landscaped front yards of buildings that are set back and that contain stoops and porches oriented to those yards.

para.heading: Housing types.
para.text: The R-6 District is meant to accommodate single-family units in both detached and semi-detached dwellings, rowhouse developments, and multi-family developments of a moderate density.

para.heading: Neighborhoods.
para.text: The R-7 Mixed Residential Zoning District is intended for those areas that offer a diverse range of housing types. Development in this district accommodates a transition between naturalistic and urban residential settings.

para.heading: Housing types.
para.text: The R-7 District is meant to accommodate a diverse range of housing types, including detached and semi-detached dwellings, rowhouse developments, and multi-family developments of a larger scale than found in the more restrictive residential districts.

para.heading: Neighborhoods.
para.text: The R-8 Rowhouse Residential Zoning District is intended to accommodate and maintain the traditional form of urban rowhouse development typical of many of the City's inner neighborhoods, which contain continuous, block-long rowhouse development built to or only modestly set back from the street.

para.heading: Housing types.
para.text: Although rowhouse is the predominant housing type, this district also accommodates other residential types, of a similar density, including detached and semi-detached dwellings, and multi-family developments of a larger scale than found in more restrictive zoning districts.

para.heading: Neighborhoods.
para.text: The R-9 Multi-Family Residential Zoning District is intended for those areas with significant green space surrounding development, particularly higher density housing and non-residential uses.

para.heading: Housing types.
para.text: The R-9 District contains a mix of higher density, but predominantly mid-rise, housing types. Permitted housing types include single-family homes, both detached and semi-detached, rowhouse developments, and multi-family developments, all with significant front yard open space. Characteristic of this district are multi-family developments sited with significant front yard open space and rowhouse developments with open space both along the perimeter of the site and within the development.

section.heading: R-10 High-Density Residential District.
section.text: The R-10 High-Density Residential Zoning District is intended for areas of significant density accommodated in concentrated high rise and rowhouse development environments.

section.heading: As listed in Table 9-301.
section.text: Only those uses of land listed in Table 9-301: Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Districts – Permitted and Conditional Uses are allowed within these zoning districts.

section.heading: In general.
section.text: Table 9-401: Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Districts – Bulk and Yard Regulations sets forth the applicable bulk and yard regulations for these zoning districts.

para.heading: Measurement methodologies.
para.text: Measurement methodologies are as set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 3 {"Measurement Methodologies"} of this Code.

para.heading: Exceptions and requirements.
para.text: Exceptions and requirements are as set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 4 {"Exceptions and Requirements"} of this Code.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Multi-family dwellings designed with a courtyard are permitted a reduction of the front yard requirement.

para.heading: Requirements.
para.text: Front yards may be reduced for courtyard building design as long as:
no more than 75% of the building's frontage maintains a minimum front yard of 15 feet;
the remaining frontage meets the minimum required front yard or 30 feet, whichever is greater; and
those portions of the courtyard building located at a reduced front yard are evenly spaced or within 10% of even spacing.

section.heading: Where allowed.
section.text: In the Residence Districts, the conversion of a single-family dwelling to a multi-family dwelling is allowed only in the R-7, R-8, R-9, and R-10 Districts, subject to:

para.text: the requirements of this subtitle; and
in the R-7 and R-8 Districts, conditional-use approval by Ordinance of the Mayor and City Council.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Design review approval is required if exterior modifications are proposed.

para.heading: Construction drawings and plans.
para.text: As part of the submittal for design review, construction drawings and plans that describe the proposed conversion in detail are required.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: All conversions must meet the standards set forth in this section.
The existing dwelling must be:
a structure originally constructed as a single-family dwelling; and
1,500 square feet or more in gross floor area.
For purposes of this subsection, gross floor area does not include any basement area.

para.heading: GFA per dwelling unit.
para.text: The converted dwelling must meet the following gross floor area per unit type:

para.heading: Bulk and yard regulations.
para.text: The dwelling must continue to conform to the applicable bulk and yard regulations, including lot area per dwelling unit, for the district in which the building is located.

para.heading: Occupancy regulations.
para.text: No residential conversion may violate any dwelling unit occupancy regulations or restrictions of the City Code.

para.heading: Off-street parking.
para.text: At least 1 off-street parking space must be provided for each dwelling unit.

para.heading: Residential character.
para.text: Following the conversion, the exterior of the dwelling must retain its existing residential character.

section.heading: In general.
section.text: The Rowhouse and Multi-Family Residential Zoning Districts are also subject to the standards listed in this subtitle.

section.heading: Accessory structures and uses.
section.text: Standards governing accessory structures and uses are set forth in Title 15, Subtitle 5 {"Accessory Structures and Uses"} of this Code.

section.heading: Site development.
section.text: On-site development standards are set forth in Title 15 {"Site Development Standards"} of this Code.

section.heading: Off-street parking and loading.
section.text: Standards governing off-street parking and loading are set forth in Title 16 {"Off-Street Parking and Loading"} of this Code.

section.heading: Design standards.
section.text: All developments of the type described in § 4-405 {"Design Review: Applicability"} of this Code must comply with the applicable design standards required by the Baltimore City Design Manual.

section.heading: Landscaping and screening.
section.text: All landscaping and screening must comply with the requirements of the Baltimore City Landscape Manual.

section.heading: Signs.
section.text: Standards governing signs are set forth in Title 17 {"Signs"} of this Code.

section.heading: Temporary uses.
section.text: Standards governing temporary uses are set forth in Title 14, Subtitle 4 {"Temporary-Use Standards"} of this Code.

section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: The purpose of this title is to set out the use regulations and the bulk and yard regulations for Commercial Zoning Districts.

para.heading: Areas for which intended.
para.text: The C-1 Neighborhood Business Zoning District is intended for areas of commercial clusters or pedestrian-oriented corridors of commercial uses that serve the immediate neighborhood.

para.heading: Standards.
para.text: The C-1 District standards are crafted to:
ensure compatibility between neighboring residential and commercial uses;
maintain the proper scale of commercial use; and
address the unique issues related to smaller commercial sites.

section.heading: C-1-E Neighborhood Business and Entertainment District.

para.heading: Areas for which intended.
para.text: The C-1-E Neighborhood Business and Entertainment Zoning District is intended for areas of commercial clusters or pedestrian-oriented corridors of commercial uses that serve the immediate neighborhood and allow for clustering of entertainment uses.

para.heading: Standards.
para.text: The C-1-E District standards are crafted to:
ensure compatibility among neighboring residential, commercial, and entertainment uses;
maintain the proper scale of commercial use; and
