The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may grant an extension of this period.

para.heading: Effect of failure to act timely.
para.text: If a building permit is not obtained within the time required by this section or the repairs not completed within 1 year of the issuance of the building permit, then the use may not be reestablished unless the structure and the use conform to all regulations of the district in which they are located.
A nonconforming structure or use may not be relocated, in whole or in part, to any other location on the same lot.

A nonconforming freestanding pole sign that is 300 square feet or larger that is either damaged or destroyed pursuant to § 18-304(a) may be relocated by no more than 15 feet in any direction from its original location.

para.heading: To another lot.
para.text: A nonconforming use may be relocated to another lot only if the use conforms to all regulations of the zoning district in which the new lot is located, including all use regulations.

para.heading: Change described.
para.text: A change of use occurs when an existing nonconforming use has been terminated and another use has commenced.

para.heading: When change allowed.
para.text: A nonconforming use may not be changed to any other use except one that is allowed within the zoning district in which it is located.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: When a nonconforming use has been changed, in whole or in part, to an allowed use, the whole or part that has been made to conform may not later be changed back to a nonconforming use.

para.heading: Exceptions.
para.text: In the R-1A, R-1B, R-1C, R-1D, R1-E, R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-4 zoning districts the zoning administrator may authorize the reestablishment of a residential nonconforming multifamily use that has lapsed up to the same number of units or a number less than the number of units that were legally established, if:
the unit was a legally established multi-family dwelling unit; and
the structure was not altered to become a single-family dwelling unit.

para.heading: Violation constitutes abandonment.
para.text: Any change in use that violates this Code constitutes an abandonment of the previously existing nonconforming use.

para.heading: Discontinuance of use.
para.text: Whenever the active and continuous operation of any nonconforming use, or any part of that use, has been discontinued for 12 consecutive months:

the discontinuance constitutes an abandonment of the discontinued nonconforming use, or discontinued part of that use, regardless of any reservation of an intent to resume active operations or otherwise not abandon the use; and
the discontinued nonconforming use, or discontinued part of that use:
may not be reestablished; and

any subsequent use of any part of the land or structure previously used for the discontinued use, or discontinued part of that use, must conform to the regulations of the district in which the land or structure is located.

para.heading: Abandonment of use.
para.text: If, at any time, actual abandonment in fact is evidenced by removal of structures, machinery, or equipment, or by alterations that indicate a change in the use of any part of the land or structure:
that action constitutes an abandonment of the nonconforming use, or affected part of that use; and
all rights to continue or reestablish the nonconforming use, or part of that use, immediately terminate.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: If a person reasonably believes that a nonconforming use has been, in whole or in part, discontinued or abandoned as described under this section, the person may file a report with the Zoning Administrator.

para.heading: Contents.
para.text: The report shall contain:
the location of the discontinued or abandoned use;
a description of the discontinued or abandoned use;
the date the person last observed the use;
a statement by the person affirming that the person reasonably believes the use describe in subparagraph (ii) of this paragraph has not occurred in the past 12 months; and
the signature or signatures of the person reporting the discontinued or abandoned use.

para.heading: Zoning Administrator to investigate.
para.text: Upon receipt of a complaint issued under this subsection, the Zoning Administrator shall inspect structures and uses of land to determine compliance with this Code and, where violations are found, initiate action to secure compliance.

section.heading: Junk or scrap storage and yards; Vehicle dismantling facilities; Landfills.

para.heading: Status.
para.text: A junk or scrap storage and yard, a vehicle dismantling facility, or a landfill lawfully existing as of June 5, 2017, is considered a lawful nonconforming conditional use, subject to the conditions and restrictions previously imposed.

para.heading: Modifications – Junk ... yards; Vehicle dismantling.
para.text: For a lawful nonconforming junk or scrap storage and yard or a lawful nonconforming vehicle dismantling facility:
structural alterations are permitted; and
an expansion of no more than 25% in land area is allowed if, in addition to any conditions and restrictions previously imposed:
the expansion is onto a property that is no more than 750 feet from the property line of the junk or scrap storage and yard or the vehicle dismantling facility; and
the expansion is onto the portion of that property that is closest to the existing use.

para.heading: Modifications – Landfills.
para.text: For a lawful nonconforming landfill:
structural alterations are permitted; and
an expansion of no more than 35% in land area is allowed if, in addition to any conditions and restrictions previously imposed:
the expansion is onto a property that is no more than 750 feet from the property line of the landfill; and
the expansion is onto the portion of that property that is closest to the existing use.

para.heading: Lot subdivision or consolidation.
para.text: The area to be used for the expansion must be subdivided into a separate lot or, if possible, consolidated as part of the existing junk or scrap storage and yard, vehicle dismantling facility, or landfill to avoid having a use allowed on a portion of a lot but not on the whole lot.

para.heading: Subtitle inapplicable to nonconforming signs.
para.text: This subtitle does not apply to nonconforming signs. Nonconforming signs are instead regulated by Subtitle 5 of this title.

para.heading: Nonconforming structure devoted to nonconforming use.

para.text: If a nonconforming structure is also devoted in whole or in part to a nonconforming use, the structure is subject to both:
the provisions of this title that govern nonconforming uses; and
the provisions of this subtitle.
In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions that govern nonconforming uses and the provisions of this subtitle, the provisions that govern nonconforming uses control.

section.heading: Continuation.
section.text: Except as otherwise specified in this Code, nonconforming structures may be continued, subject to the requirements of this subtitle.

section.heading: Expansion of structure.
section.text: A nonconforming structure may not be expanded if the expansion would, create a new nonconformity or increase the degree of any nonconformity.

para.heading: Maintenance and repairs.
para.text: Normal maintenance and incidental repair may be performed on any nonconforming structure, as long as the maintenance or repair will not, in any way, create any new nonconformity, increase the degree of any nonconformity, or increase the bulk of the structure.

para.heading: Structural alterations.
para.text: No structural alterations may be performed on any nonconforming structure, unless:
the alteration is required by law;
the alteration is necessary to restore the structure to a safe condition on order of any official charged with protecting the public safety;
the alteration will result in eliminating the nonconformity; or
the alteration will not, in any way, create any new nonconformity, increase the degree of any nonconformity, or increase the bulk of the structure.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: If a nonconforming structure is damaged or destroyed, the structure may be repaired or reconstructed as long as no new nonconformities are created and the existing degree of nonconformity is not increased.
A building permit must be obtained for the repair or reconstruction within 2 years of the date of the damage or destruction.
The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may grant an extension of this period.

para.heading: Effect of failure to act timely.
para.text: If the building permit is not obtained within the time required by this section or the repairs not completed within 1 year of the issuance of the building permit, then the structure may not be restored unless the structure conforms to all regulations of the district in which it is located.

section.heading: Relocation.
section.text: A nonconforming structure may not be moved, in whole or in part, to any other location on the lot, unless the structure or the moved part of the structure is made to comply with the bulk and yard regulations of the district in which the structure is located.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: A minor expansion of a nonconforming structure may be made with the administrative approval of the Zoning Administrator, as provided in this section.
An application under this section must be filed by the property owner or with the written consent of the property owner.
The application must be filed with the Zoning Administrator, in the form and with the information and accompanying plans that the Zoning Administrator requires.
The application must include a certification by the property owner:
that the structure is a nonconforming structure; and
that a copy of the application has been given to the owners of the adjoining properties.
On receipt of an application, the Zoning Administrator must promptly refer it to the Director of Planning for design review.

para.heading: Review and approval.
para.text: The Planning Director may recommend approval of the application if, after design review, the Director finds that the proposal:
is in harmony with the general character, arrangement, design, and architectural features of similar buildings within a radius of 300 feet;
is not contrary to the public interest; and
is consistent with the purposes and intent of this Code.

para.heading: Imposition of conditions.
para.text: To the extent necessary or desirable to reduce or minimize any effect of a proposed expansion on other properties in the neighborhood, the Planning Director may recommend:
requiring changes in any design or plan of any existing structure or any alteration of the structure; and
imposing conditions, restrictions, and limitations governing:
screening or fencing;
type of lighting; and
any other relevant matter.
A copy of the Planning Director's recommendation on the application must be filed with the Zoning Administrator.

When issued, the Director's decision constitutes a recommendation to the Zoning Administrator. The Zoning Administrator's decision is a final decision for purposes of administrative appeal under Title 19, Subtitle 3 {"Administrative and Judicial Review"} of this Code.
Failure to comply with any change, condition, restriction, or limitation imposed under this section constitutes a violation of this Code.
No condition, restriction, or limitation imposed under this section may be changed unless, on the filing of a new application, that change is authorized under this section.
Except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, this section applies to any structure that:

at any time, with or without authorization of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, has been converted for 4 or more dwelling units or, if originally built for 4 or more dwelling units, has been converted to increase the number of dwelling units; and
now fails to comply with the minimum lot area requirements of the district in which it is located.
This section does not apply to any nonconforming structure that:
in compliance with this Code or before June 5, 2017, was originally designed and built as a multi-family dwelling for 4 or more dwelling units, as evidenced by permits or records of the City; and
has not been altered, added to, or subdivided in any way that increases the number of dwelling units to more than the maximum now allowed under this Code.

para.heading: Discontinuance of dwelling unit.
para.text: Whenever the active and continuous use of a dwelling unit in a nonconforming multi-family structure subject to this section has been discontinued for 12 consecutive months:
the discontinuance constitutes an abandonment of that dwelling unit, regardless of any reservation of an intent to resume active use of or to reoccupy the unit or otherwise not to abandon it; and
the number of dwelling units allowed to continue in the structure is reduced by 1.

para.heading: Abandonment of dwelling unit.
para.text: If, at any time, actual abandonment is in fact is evidenced by removal of plumbing or kitchen facilities, by alterations that indicate an abandonment of any nonconforming dwelling unit, including consolidation with another dwelling unit, or by the issuance of a use permit for fewer dwelling units:
that action constitutes an abandonment of the dwelling unit;
all rights to continue or reestablish the previous number of dwelling units immediately terminate; and
the number of dwelling units allowed to continue in the structure is reduced by 1.

para.heading: Exceptions.
para.text: This section does not apply to § 18-306(c) {"Change of use . . . Reversion prohibited."} of this Code.

section.heading: Structures in Hospital Campus District.
section.text: All lawfully existing structures that, as of June 5, 2017, are located in a Hospital Campus Zoning District are considered to be conforming structures.

section.heading: In general.
section.text: Signs that were lawful when erected but no longer conform to the requirements of this Code must comply with the following regulations.

section.heading: Alterations, replacements, relocations, etc.
section.text: Any nonconforming sign may be structurally altered, reconstructed, replaced, or relocated, as long as the alteration, reconstruction, replacement, or relocation does not result in:

para.text: an increase in the area or any dimension of the sign;
an increase in the degree of illumination of the sign;
the addition of:
any moving, rotating or otherwise animated part; or
any flashing, blinking, fluctuating, or otherwise animated light; or
any other increase in the degree of the sign's nonconformity.

section.heading: Restoration of damaged signs.
section.text: If a nonconforming sign is damaged or destroyed to the extent of more than 50% of the sign's fair market value immediately preceding the damage, the sign may not be repaired or reconstructed unless it will then conform to all applicable regulations for the district.

section.heading: Continuance of certain nonconforming billboards.
section.text: Any legal nonconforming billboard, as of June 5, 2017, may continue to follow the rule in § 11-207(c)(9) and (10) of the Zoning Code of Baltimore City that was in effect on June 4, 2017.

para.heading: Scope.
para.text: This section does not apply in an Industrial District.

para.heading: When allowed.
para.text: On a nonconforming lot that was established before June 5, 2017, a single-family dwelling may be erected regardless of the minimum lot area requirements imposed by this Code as long as:
the nonconforming lot meets all other requirements of this Code; and
the owner of the nonconforming lot does not also own any abutting lot that can be consolidated with the nonconforming lot.

section.heading: Retail goods establishment – with alcoholic beverage sales.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, retail goods establishments with alcoholic beverage sales in a residential district must be terminated as follows:

for an establishment with alcoholic beverage sales that existed as a lawful nonconforming use before June 5, 2017, no later than June 4, 2019, notwithstanding the issuance of any prior use permit as a nonconforming package goods liquor store; and

for an establishment that becomes nonconforming on or after June 5, 2017, whether by the enactment of this Code, by the enactment of an amendment to this Code, or by the reclassification of the property, no later than 3 years after the date on which the use became nonconforming.

para.heading: Board Authority.
para.text: The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may extend by an additional 2 years the time by which a retail goods establishment with alcoholic beverage sales must terminate the nonconforming use.

para.heading: Timely application.
para.text: To obtain an extension, the property owner or lessee must apply to the Board, in writing, within 1 year after the effective date of this Code (June 5, 2017), of the amendment to this Code, or of the property reclassification, as the case may be.

For nonconforming uses existing before June 5, 2017, the property owner or lessee seeking an extension must establish the existence of one of the following factors that would render termination within the time required by subsection (a) of this section a hardship:
purchase of the property after January 1, 2008, and before April 1, 2012;
investment in capital improvements to the property in excess of $100,000 after June 30, 2007, and before April 1, 2012; or
a lease that was entered into before April 1, 2012, has a term remaining in excess of 10 years, and is not terminable by the lessee because of zoning changes prohibiting the use.

For all other uses that become nonconforming, whether by enactment of this Code, by the enactment of an amendment to this Code, or by reclassification of the property, the property owner or lessee seeking an extension must establish the existence of one of the following factors that would render termination within the time required by subsection (a) of this section a hardship:

purchase of the property within the 5 years immediately preceding the enactment of this Code, the enactment of the amendment to this Code, or the enactment of the property reclassification, as the case may be;
investment in capital improvements to the property in excess of $100,000 after June 30, 2007, and before April 1, 2012; or
a lease that was entered into before April 1, 2012, has a term remaining in excess of 10 years, and is not terminable by the lessee because of zoning changes prohibiting the use.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Nonconforming taverns must either:
fully comply with § 14-337 {"Taverns"} within 2 years after they become nonconforming; or
be terminated.

para.heading: Waiver for hardship.
para.text: A waiver extending the time for compliance based on hardship may be applied for in accordance with § 18-701(b) {"Retail good establishments...: Waiver for hardship"} of this subtitle.

container.heading: Prohibited Conduct; Enforcement; Administrative and Judicial Review

section.heading: Prohibited conduct.
section.text: No person may:

para.text: violate any provision of this Code, of any rule, regulation, or manual adopted under this Code, or of any permit, notice, or order issued under this Code;

refuse, neglect, omit, or otherwise fail to comply with any provision of this Code, of any rule, regulation, or manual adopted under this Code, or of any permit, notice, or order issued under this Code;
resist the enforcement of any provision of this Code, of any rule, regulation, or manual adopted under this Code, or of any notice or order issued under this Code; or
cause any of these acts or omissions to be done.

section.heading: Each day a separate offense.
section.text: Each day that a violation continues after written notice from the Zoning Administrator constitutes a separate offense.

section.heading: "Person responsible" defined.
section.text: In this subtitle, "person responsible" means any owner, operator, manager, or tenant of a property or use subject to this Code, or any other person responsible for or having the care, control, or possession of that property or use, whether as a principal or as an agent, personal representative, trustee, guardian, or otherwise, and whether alone or jointly with any other person.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Whenever the Zoning Administrator learns of a violation of § 19-101 {"Prohibited conduct"} of this Code, the Zoning Administrator may issue a violation notice to:
the owner of record of the property, as shown on the tax records of Baltimore City; and
any other person who the Zoning Administrator has reason to believe is a person responsible for the violation.

para.heading: Contents of notice.
para.text: The notice must:
specify the location and nature of the violation;
cite the provisions of this Code or of the rules, regulations, manual, permit, notice, or order that have been violated;
state the requirements that must be complied with to rectify the violation and the time within which the violation must be rectified; and
advise the recipient of the right to request a hearing within 10 days of the date on which the notice was served.

para.heading: Compliance required.
para.text: On receipt of a violation notice from the Zoning Administrator, the recipient must immediately take appropriate steps to correct the violation.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: Except as otherwise specified in this Code, all notices issued by the Zoning Administrator must be served on:
the person for whom the notice is intended; or
an authorized agent or representative of that person.

para.heading: More than 1 person responsible.
para.text: If more than 1 person is responsible for the violation or otherwise responsible for complying with this Code, as in a case of property owned by more than 1 person, notice may be served on any 1 of those persons or on any authorized agent or representative of any of them.

para.heading: Method of service – In general.
para.text: A notice is properly served on a person if:
served personally on that person (or on that person's authorized agent or representative);
hand-delivered to the home or business address of that person (or of that person's authorized agent or representative); or
sent by certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, to the home or business address of that person (or of that person's authorized agent or representative).

para.heading: Method of service – Posting.
para.text: Adequate and sufficient notice may be made by posting a copy of the notice on the property in question if:
the identity or whereabouts of the person responsible is unknown; or

a notice that was hand-delivered or mailed under subsection (c) of this section is refused, returned unclaimed, or designated undeliverable by the post office for any reason, and neither of the following sources can provide a more accurate address:
the tax records of the City's Bureau of Treasury Management, Collections Division; and
the property registration files of the Department of Housing and Community Development.

section.heading: Extension of time limit.
section.text: The Zoning Administrator may extend the time within which to comply with a violation notice if, in the Administrator's judgment, more time is needed to comply.

para.heading: Administrator may seek.
para.text: If a violation is not promptly discontinued and rectified or if a violation notice is not complied with promptly, the Zoning Administrator may institute or cause to be instituted any appropriate civil or criminal action or proceeding to secure compliance.

para.heading: Types of proceedings.
para.text: These enforcement proceedings include:
civil court proceedings (see § 19-213);
service of citations (see § 19-214; and
criminal prosecution (see § 19-215).

section.heading: Remedies not exclusive.
section.text: In pursuing a violation, the Zoning Administrator may use any one or more available remedies or enforcement actions. The initiation of any one remedy or enforcement action does not preclude pursuing any other remedy or enforcement action authorized by law.

para.heading: In general.
para.text: The Zoning Administrator, on behalf of the Mayor and City Council, may file a petition in District Court to compel compliance with or obtain other relief under this Code.

para.heading: Judicial relief.
para.text: In an action brought under this section, the court may compel compliance with this Code by:
issuing an order to cease and desist from a violation; and
granting other injunctive relief, as appropriate to:
prevent unlawful construction;
restrain, correct, or abate a violation;
prevent illegal occupancy of a structure or premises; or
stop an illegal act, conduct, business, or use of a structure on or about any premises.

para.heading: Civil fines and costs.
para.text: In an action brought under this section, the court may also:
impose a civil fine of up to $500 for each day that a violation continues; and
award to the City reasonable enforcement costs and attorney's fees, whether or not the attorney is a salaried employee of the City.

section.heading: Enforcement by citation.
section.text: In addition to any other civil or criminal remedy or enforcement procedure, this Code may be enforced by issuance of the following:

para.text: an environmental citation under City Code Article 1, Subtitle 40 {"Environmental Control Board"};
a civil citation under City Code Article 1, Subtitle 41 {"Civil Citations"}; and
a pre-payable criminal citation under City Code Article 19, Subtitle 71 {"Special Enforcement Officers"}.

section.heading: Criminal penalties.
section.text: Any person who violates any provision of § 19-101 {"Prohibited conduct"} of this title is guilty of a misdemeanor and, on conviction, is subject to a fine of not more than $500 or imprisonment for not more than 30 days or both fine and imprisonment for each offense.

para.heading: Who may appeal.
para.text: A decision of the Zoning Administrator, including the issuance of a violation notice under Subtitle 2 {"Enforcement"} of this title, may be appealed to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals by:
any person aggrieved by the decision; or
any officer or department, board, bureau, or other unit of the City affected by the decision.
The notice of appeal must be filed as follows:
in the case of a violation notice, within 10 days of the date the notice was served; and
in the case of any other decision, within 10 days of the date on which notice of the decision was given.
The notice of appeal must:
be filed with the Zoning Administrator, in the form that the rules of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals require; and
specify the grounds for the appeal.

Once the Zoning Administrator determines the notice of appeal is timely and complete, the Zoning Administrator must transmit the notice to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals, together with all information that constitutes the record of the action appealed from.

If the appeal is timely filed and pursued, an appeal to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals stays all proceedings in furtherance of the action appealed from, except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection.

If the Zoning Administrator certifies to the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals that, by reason of facts stated in the certification, a stay would, in his or her opinion, cause imminent peril to life or property or is not justified by any material fact, the proceedings are not stayed, unless otherwise ordered by the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals or, on application to a court of competent jurisdiction, with notice to the Zoning Administrator, by the court on good cause shown.

Within 30 days of the public hearing, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must render its decision in writing, setting forth its findings of fact and conclusions of law. If, however, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals determines that additional time is needed to render a decision, the Board may, on written notice to the parties, extend the time for an additional 30 days.
In exercising its powers of review, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may:
reverse or affirm, wholly or in part, or modify the decision appealed from; and
make any order, requirement, decision, or determination as ought to be made in accordance with this Code.
For these purposes, the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals has all the powers conferred by this Code on the Zoning Administrator.

para.heading: Final administrative decision.
para.text: All decisions and findings of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals that are made on appeals, on application for conditional uses or variances, and in all other matters on which the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals is required to act after public notice and hearing, are final administrative decisions, subject to judicial review.

para.heading: Who may seek.
para.text: Judicial review of a final administrative decision of the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals may be sought by:
any person aggrieved by the decision; or
any officer or department, board, bureau, or other unit of the City aggrieved by the decision.
This review must be sought within the time and in the manner required by law and the Maryland Rules of Procedure.
Before the petition for judicial review is filed with the court, the petitioner must file a copy with the Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals and the Zoning Administrator.
The Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals must promptly notify the City Solicitor of the filing of every petition for judicial review.
The filing of a petition for judicial review does not stay the proceedings for which the review is sought.
On motion and hearing, the court may grant a stay on good cause shown, subject to the conditions of bond or otherwise that the court considers proper.

section.heading: Appellate review.
section.text: Any party to the judicial review may appeal the court's final judgment to the Court of Special Appeals in accordance with the Maryland Rules of Procedure.

attachment.heading: Canton Waterfront Area

img.alt: A map of the Canton Waterfront Area. The map displays the W-1 Waterfront Overlay District, Height Control Zones including Areas 1 through 4, Public Access Corridors, and Harbor. If you need additional assistance, please contact the Department of Planning at (410) 396-7526.

attachment.text: Height Limitations - The height of structures along the waterfront may not exceed 35 feet, except in Areas 1 through 4. Height controls are provided in Areas 1 through 4 to minimize the impact of building heights on adjacent neighborhoods. Specific locations for higher buildings are provided, as well as guidelines for building setbacks and stepbacks. The maximum building height shall be defined as the vertical distance measured, in the case of flat roofs, from the mean curb level of the highest point of the roof adjacent to the street wall, and in the case of pitched roofs, from the mean curb level to the mean height level of the roof. Where the walls of a building are not adjacent to a street curb, the height of a building shall be measured from the average elevation of the ground adjoining the walls.

td.p: Average height of the built area may not exceed 45 feet.
Maximum building height shall be 50 feet.

Maximum building height along Aliceanna Street, Chester Street, and the water's edge shall be 40 feet. Additional height above 40 feet up to the maximum of 50 feet shall be constructed so that it is not visible from that portion of the promenade adjacent to the area or shall step up at an angle of no more than 45 degrees. The building shall be setback a minimum of 20 feet from the Chester Street right-of-way.
Average height of the built area may not exceed 65 feet.
Maximum height, excluding HVAC or other mechanical systems, is 75 feet. Maximum height for the HVAC and other mechanical systems may not exceed 90 feet.

The maximum building height on Boston Street, the northwest and the water's edge shall be 60 feet. Additional height above 60 feet up to the maximum of 75 feet shall be constructed so it is not visible from that portion of the promenade adjacent to the area and from the sidewalk on the north side of Boston Street adjacent to the area or shall step up at an angle of no more than 45 degrees.
The water's edge shall have a maximum height of 40 feet.

Additional height above 40 feet up to a maximum height no higher than the existing properties at 2351- 2439 Boston Street shall be constructed so that it is not visible from that portion of the promenade adjacent to the area or shall step up at an angle of no more than 45 degrees.
Average height of the built area may not exceed 50 feet.
The water's edge shall have a maximum height of 40 feet. Additional height above 40 feet shall be setback at an angle of no more than 45 degrees up to 79 feet.

attachment.text: Public Access Corridors - Minimum width of the corridors shall be 50 feet, unless otherwise noted below. Landscaping, trees, lights, benches, tables, and other public amenities that will enhance, not impede, public view of the water shall be permitted. All access corridors should connect sidewalk and promenade and be physically and visually uninterrupted. In cases where a public access corridor is to be located between 2 properties, the center of the corridor shall be on the property line and the width of the corridor shall be evenly divided between the 2 properties.

tr.td: From a point at the approximate intersection of Boston and Aliceanna Streets south to the water between 2201 and 2121 Boston Street.

A 30 foot wide public access corridor shall be designated between 2301 Boston Street (North shore) and 2351 Boston Street (Anchorage Townhomes), consisting of a 15 foot wide public access corridor each on 2301 Boston Street and 2351 Boston Street.
A 15-foot wide public access corridor shall be designated between 2369 and 2371, between 2389 and 2401, and between 2419 and 2421 Boston Street.
A 30-foot wide public access corridor shall be designated between 2439 and 2449 Boston Street.

From a point at the approximate intersection of Luzerne Avenue and Hudson Street due south along the axis of Luzerne Avenue to the waterfront park. In the Luzerne Avenue corridor, if financially necessary and subject to the review and approval of the Commissioner of Housing and Community Development, a second level pedestrian bridge may be allowed.
From a point at the approximate intersection of Lakewood Avenue and Boston Street due south along the axis of Lakewood Avenue through to the water.
From a point at the approximate intersection of Kenwood Avenue and Boston Street along the axis of the existing 2809 Boston Street approximately southwest to the water.
From a point at the approximate intersection of Linwood Avenue and Boston Street along the axis of the existing 2809 Boston Street approximately southwest to the water.

This public access corridor shall be described by a set of parallel lines. The northern line shall extend west from the intersection of Elliott Street and Kenwood Avenue along the north axis of Elliott Street to the water; the southern will be parallel and 50 feet south of the above line.

attachment.text: Height Limitations - The maximum building height shall be defined as the vertical distance measured, in the case of flat roofs, from the mean curb level of the highest point of the roof adjacent to the street wall, and in the case of pitched roofs, from the mean curb level to the mean height level of the roof. Where the walls of a building are not adjacent to a street curb, the height of a building shall be measured from the average elevation of the ground adjoining the walls.

The maximum building heights shall be as set forth in the Constellation PUD.

Thames Street elevations may be no higher than 40 feet. A building addition up to a maximum of 53 feet will be permitted if it is set back and designed so that it is not visible from the street frontage opposite this area.
Maximum building height may not exceed 40 feet.

Maximum building height may not exceed 60 feet, except on the property known as 1000 Fell Street where rehabilitation of the roof structure to accommodate a seventh story is permitted, provided that this seventh story is recessed so as not to be seen from the street frontage of the subject property, and a further exception is provided for the property known as 932-944 Fell Street (Belt's Wharf Condominium Property) for a building addition up to a maximum of 74 feet if recessed 40 feet from the street frontage of the property.

The average height of built area may be no more than 50 feet, with a maximum height of 60 feet. The maximum height along the water's edge is 40 feet. Additional height over 40 feet up to the maximum of 60 feet shall be constructed so that it is not visible from that portion of the promenade adjacent to the area or shall step up at an angle of no more than 45 degrees.

The average height of built area may be no more than 75 feet, with a maximum height of 90 feet. The maximum height along Wolfe Street and the water's edge is 40 feet. The maximum height along Thames Street is 60 feet. Additional height over the 40 feet and 60 feet up to the maximum of 90 feet shall be constructed so that it is not visible from that portion of the promenade adjacent to the area, Wolfe Street or Thames Street or shall step up at an angle of no more than 45 degrees.

The average height of built area shall be 45 feet, with a maximum height of 65 feet. The maximum height on Aliceanna Street, Chester Street and the water side shall be 40 feet for a minimum of 40 feet depth. The building shall be set back a minimum of 20 feet from the Chester Street right-of-way. Additions to the existing building at 705 S. Wolfe Street are permitted up to 65 feet. These additions shall be set back so as not to be seen from Wolfe Street, Aliceanna Street and the promenade adjacent to the area.

attachment.text: Public Access Corridors - In order to assure public access to the Pedestrian Promenade and to preserve and enhance views of the water, the following public access corridors shall be designated. The minimum width of the corridors shall be 50 feet. Landscaping, trees, lights, benches, tables, and other public amenities that will enhance, not impede, public view of the water shall be permitted. Off-street parking is not permitted within these corridors, except following review and approval of the Commissioner of the Department of Housing and Community Development. All access corridors should connect sidewalk and promenade and be physically and visually uninterrupted, and they must be accessible 24 hours daily. The general location of the following public access corridors are shown on the accompanying exhibit.

td.p: Priority Open Space Bonus: additional height and density above 140 feet may be earned for the
